properties.name: Geometry
properties.desc: Gets the container used by the icon to store its geometry.

properties.name: Layer
properties.desc: Defines the layer the icon belongs to in the 3D world.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the icon's name.

properties.name: Uri
properties.desc: Defines the URI of the icon file.

methods.name: createProperty
methods.desc:
Adds a new user-defined property of a given type 
		 and name to action, and then returns 
		 the new property. 
		An optional constraints 
		 argument can be given to define the constraints of the property, 
		 which must be given at the time of creation.
		See Property constants 
		 for available property types and constraints.

methods.name: deleteProperty
methods.desc: Deletes a given property from action.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc:
Returns the first property matching a given name 
		 in action; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: send
methods.desc:
Sends action to the defined container. 
		 
		If no arguments are given, the action is 
		 broadcast to all connected Action Containers.

methods.name: sendMessage
methods.desc:
Sends action with a given message 
		 to all connected Action Containers. 
		An optional container 
		 argument can be given to specify which action container receives 
		 the action.
		Generally, the message of an action defines 
		 the action's type and is used by an action container to execute 
		 the action. In some cases, the message is used to filter actions.

properties.name: ActionContainer
properties.desc: Gets the action container of action.

properties.name: ActionTime
properties.desc: Gets the creation time of action.

properties.name: AllProperties
properties.desc: Gets a list of all user-defined properties for the action.

properties.name: Filter
properties.desc:
Defines a filter for limiting what resource can perform the 
		 action.

properties.name: From
properties.desc:
Defines the original sender of this action. 
		Generally, this is used to track and manipulate 
		 where an action is sent from. For example, an action might be 
		 forwarded and passed to different resources and task managers.

properties.name: Message
properties.desc: Defines the status information about the action's execution.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of action.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc:
Gets a list of all user-defined properties created for the 
		 action after the action container was loaded.

properties.name: Receiver
properties.desc:
Defines the receiver of action in its current workflow. 
		For example, an action might need to be 
		 handled at a workstation before the action is sent to a target 
		 defined by its To property.

properties.name: Sender
properties.desc:
Defines the current sender of the action. 
		Generally, this is used to clearly identify 
		 which object is responsible for sending this action.

properties.name: To
properties.desc:
Defines the final target where the action should be sent to. 
		 
		In some cases, an action's final destination 
		 might be redefined to handle issues such as quality inspections, 
		 rerouting of materials, and availability of resource providers.

methods.name: clear
methods.desc: Deletes all actions in container.

methods.name: clearPending
methods.desc: Deletes all pending actions in container.

methods.name: createAction
methods.desc:
Creates a new vcAction 
		 in container, and then returns the new action.

methods.name: createPendingAction
methods.desc: Creates a new pending action in the container.

methods.name: deleteAction
methods.desc:
Deletes a given action or one at 
		 a given index from container. 
		If deletion is successful, returns True; 
		 otherwise returns False.

methods.name: deletePendingAction
methods.desc: Deletes a given action from the PendingActions property list.

methods.name: do
methods.desc:
Executes an action using the container. 
		If action can be performed, returns True; 
		 otherwise returns False. 
		Each action type has its own set of arguments 
		 which are described in Action 
		 Constants. Action arguments can be added in the order how 
		 they are described in the action parameter table.
		An alternative approach is to use Python 
		 keywords, which allows only using specific keyword arguments.
		See list of possible action 
		 types and their arguments.

methods.name: getAction
methods.desc:
Returns an action found at the given index 
		 in container.

methods.name: getPendingAction
methods.desc:
Returns a pending action found at a given index 
		 in container.

methods.name: getResources
methods.desc: Returns a list of immediate resources connected to container.

methods.name: moveAction
methods.desc:
Moves a given action 
		 to a given index in Actions property 
		 list. 
		If moving is successful, returns True; otherwise 
		 returns False.

methods.name: movePendingAction
methods.desc:
Moves a given action 
		 to a new position in the PendingActions property list. 
		If moving is successful, returns True, otherwise 
		 False is returned.

methods.name: popPending
methods.desc:
Removes the last action from the PendingActions property list, 
		 and then returns that action; otherwise returns None. 
		If an index 
		 argument is given, the action found at that position in the PendingActions 
		 property list will be removed and returned by the method; otherwise, 
		 returns None.

methods.name: release
removePendingAction
methods.desc:
Removes a given action 
		 from the PendingActions property list.

methods.name: reserve
methods.desc:
Reserves a resource provider matching resource_filter, 
		 and then returns the reserved resource.
		If resource is not available immediately, 
		 the method will wait until resource is available. If no matching 
		 resource is available, the method returns None. 
		An optional action_type 
		 argument can be given to reserve the resource for a specific action.
		See list of possible action 
		 types.
		An optional Timeout argument can be 
		 given to define how long the method will wait (in seconds) in 
		 order to reserve a resource. If the resource cannot be reserved 
		 before Timeout expires, 
		 the method returns None.

methods.name: start
methods.desc:
Executes an action using container regardless if an other action 
		 is still running. 
		If action can be performed, returns True; 
		 otherwise returns False.
		Generally, start() is used with the wait() 
		 method in order to catch when an action executed with start() 
		 has been completed.
		Each action type has its own set of arguments 
		 which are described in Action 
		 Constants. Action arguments can be added in the order how 
		 they are described in the action parameter table.
		An alternative approach is to use Python 
		 keywords, which allows only using specific keyword arguments.
		See list of possible action 
		 types.

methods.name: use
methods.desc:
Executes an action using a specific resource. 
		If no resource is found based on resource_filter 
		 and the action is available immediately (not in queue), the method 
		 will wait until the specified resource is available. If resource 
		 can be used to perform action, returns True; otherwise returns 
		 False.
		Optional timeout 
		 keyword argument defines how long the method will wait (in seconds) 
		 for the reserved resource to become available. If resource cannot 
		 be reserved before timeout 
		 expires, return False.
		Each action type has its own set of arguments 
		 which are described in Action 
		 Constants. Action arguments can be added in the order how 
		 they are described in the action parameter table.
		An alternative approach is to use Python 
		 keywords, which allows only using specific keyword arguments.
		See list of possible action 
		 types.

methods.name: wait
methods.desc:
Waits until action called in start() method is completed, and 
		 then returns True. 
		If an optional timeout 
		 argument is used, the method will return False if an action is 
		 not completed within the allocated time period (in seconds).

properties.name: ActionCount
properties.desc: Gets the total number of actions in container.

properties.name: Actions
properties.desc: Gets a list of all actions in container.

properties.name: Brokers
properties.desc: Defines a list of connected brokers.

properties.name: Clients
properties.desc: Defines a list of connected clients.

properties.name: PendingActionCount
properties.desc: Gets the number of actions in the PendingActions property list.

properties.name: NextFreeTime
properties.desc:
Defines the next available time this container is able to process 
		 actions during a simulation.

properties.name: PendingActions
properties.desc:
Gets a list of pending action stored in the container. That 
		 is, actions that are received from other action containers and 
		 buffered for action processing.

properties.name: Processing
properties.desc: Defines if this container is executing actions.

properties.name: Providers
properties.desc: Defines a list of connected providers.

properties.name: Reserved
properties.desc: Defines if this container is reserved by other action container.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc:
Returns a property matching a given name 
		 in the annotation; otherwise returns None.

properties.name: Height
properties.desc: Defines the height of text displayed in annotation.

properties.name: LineWidth
properties.desc: Defines the line width of annotation.

properties.name: Location
properties.desc:
Defines the position matrix of annotation in World coordinate 
		 system).

properties.name: LockToNode
properties.desc:
Defines if the annotation is attached to a node in component. 
		 That is, whether or not the annotation is anchored to a component 
		 or 3D world.

properties.name: Material
properties.desc: Defines the material of annotation.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the annotation's name.

properties.name: Node
properties.desc:
Defines the node the annotation is attached to in the 3D world. 
		 
		If the annotation is not locked to a node, 
		 the value is None.

properties.name: Position
properties.desc:
Defines the location of the annotation in its parent's coordinate 
		 system. That is, the anchor point of the annotation. 
		If the annotation is not anchored to a component, 
		 the location is based in the World (simulation root node) coordinate 
		 system.

properties.name: Text
properties.desc: Defines the text of the annotation displayed in an environment.

properties.name: Thickness
properties.desc: Defines the thickness of the annotation's text in an environment.

methods.name: loadBitmap
methods.desc:
Loads a bitmap image from a given uri. 
		 
		If loading is successful, the bitmap's filename 
		 is used to register the bitmap with the application.
		Returns the loaded bitmap image; otherwise 
		 returns None.

methods.name: saveBitmap
methods.desc:
Writes a given bitmap to a given 
		 uri. 
		By default, the bitmap is saved as a BMP 
		 file. An optional writer_info argument 
		 can be given to write the bitmap to a different format.
		rbmp writes to BMP.
		rjpegstd or rjpegnstd writes to JPEG.
		rpng writes to PNG.
		rtargareader writes to TGA.
		See vcBitmap for more information.

methods.name: findCamera
methods.desc:
Returns a camera used by the application in an environment. 
		 
		An optional name 
		 argument can be given to find a specific camera; otherwise the 
		 method returns the first found camera.
		If no camera is found, returns None.

methods.name: cancelCommand
methods.desc:
Cancels the execution of the currently active command, after 
		 which the default command of the application is activated. 
		An optional all 
		 argument of can be given to cancel all commands in the command 
		 stack or just the top-most command by giving a False value.

methods.name: deleteCommand
methods.desc: Deletes a registered command that matches a given name.

methods.name: findCommand
methods.desc:
Returns a registered command that matches a given name; 
		 otherwise returns None.

methods.name: getCommands
methods.desc: Returns a list of commands registered to the application.

methods.name: loadCommand
methods.desc:
Loads a defined script of a given name 
		 at a given uri into the application 
		 as a Python command. 
		Loading registers a command with the given 
		 name in the application, 
		 which can be used to launch the command itself. Successful command 
		 loading returns the command as an object; otherwise, returns None.

methods.name: clearWorld
methods.desc: Removes all components from the 3D world.

methods.name: cloneComponent
methods.desc:
Clones a given component, 
		 and then returns the clone. 
		Note: This is 
		 only for static components when simulation is not running. To 
		 clone components when a simulation is running, use vcComponent.clone().

methods.name: connectComponents
methods.desc:
Connects all matching interfaces between two given components. 
		 
		If a physical connection requires repositioning 
		 then comp2 is snapped to comp1.
		If a connection forms a parent-child hierarchy, 
		 the child component is moved and attached 
		 to the parent component.

methods.name: createComponent
methods.desc:
Creates a new component at the 3D world origin, and then returns 
		 the new component.

methods.name: deleteComponent
methods.desc:
Deletes a given component from 
		 the 3D world.

methods.name: findComponent
methods.desc:
Returns a component in the 3D world that matches a given name. 
		If no match is found, returns None.

methods.name: createLayout
methods.desc: Creates a new empty simulation layout.

methods.name: load
methods.desc:
Loads a component from a given uri 
		 in the 3D world. 
		If loading is successful, returns the component; 
		 otherwise returns None.
		Note: In most 
		 cases, the file URI scheme is file:/// followed by the full path 
		 to file.

methods.name: setContext
methods.desc:
Sets the context of application to the given id. 
		 
		Standard ids are:
		Author
		Component modeling
		Configure
		Layout configuration
		Drawing
		2D drawing
		Teach
		Robot programming.

methods.name: beginFrameGrab
methods.desc:
Starts frame grabbing process using given image_format, 
		 image_width and image_height 
		 arguments to use with the executeFrameGrab() method.

methods.name: endFrameGrab
methods.desc: Ends screen grabbing process and performs cleanup.

methods.name: executeFrameGrab
methods.desc:
Creates a video frame of the current 3D world view and saves 
		 the frame at a given uri. The frame's 
		 format and size are defined using the beginFrameGrab() method.

methods.name: doJogging
methods.desc:
Does the actual jogging using given vector 
		 as a reference location in world coordinates where the jogging 
		 ends.

methods.name: startJogging
methods.desc:
Initializes jogging process by defining what node 
		 is jogged and vector where 
		 the jogging starts, that is a reference starting location in the 
		 world coordinate system.

methods.name: stopJogging
methods.desc: Stops jogging.

methods.name: createLayer
methods.desc:
Creates a new layer with a given name 
		 in the application. 
		If a layer with the given name 
		 exists, that layer is returned; otherwise the method returns the 
		 new layer. If the layer cannot be created, returns None.

methods.name: deleteLayer
methods.desc:
Deletes a layer that matches a given name 
		  unless the layer is a system 
		 layer.

methods.name: findLayer
methods.desc:
Returns a layer that matches a given name; 
		 otherwise returns None.

methods.name: createLayoutItem
methods.desc:
Creates a new layout item of a given type 
		 in the current layout. 
		See Layout 
		 Item constants for types and descriptions.

methods.name: deleteLayoutItem
methods.desc:
Deletes a given layout_item or 
		 one that matches a given name from 
		 the current layout.

methods.name: findLayoutItem
methods.desc:
Returns a layout item that matches a given name 
		 in current layout; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: createLight
methods.desc:
Creates a new light with a given name 
		 which is attached to the 3D world.

methods.name: deleteLight
methods.desc: Deletes a light that matches a given name.

methods.name: findLight
methods.desc:
Returns the first found light in the 3D world or a light matching 
		 a given name. 
		If no light is found with the given name, returns None.

methods.name: addMaterial
methods.desc:
Adds a given material to a group of materials registered with 
		 the application. 
		If the material is registered, returns True. 
		 If a material with the same name already exists, returns False.

methods.name: createMaterial
methods.desc: Creates a new material with a given name.

methods.name: findMaterial
methods.desc:
Returns a material matching a given name. 
		 If no material is found with the name, 
		 returns None.
		
		Optional case_sensitive 
		 argument can 
		 be used to specify if the method is case-sensitive. By default, 
		 the method returns the first match (not case-sensitive).

methods.name: addMenuButton
methods.desc:
Adds a new menu button in the ribbon (similar to the item). 
		 The first three parameters are the same as in addMenuItem, and 
		 the toolSize parameter defines the 
		 appearance of the button.

methods.name: addUxSite
methods.desc:
Adds a new site identified by siteId at the specified position. 
		 
		siteId can be a concatenated string or a path, 
		 thereby allowing you to specify a section of the user interface.
		 For example, 'VcTabDrawing/Example' would 
		 create a new ribbon group called Example in the Drawing tab.
		Caution: You
		 can refer to the <UXSitesSection> element of your application's
		 configuration file to know valid IDs. Each id is an ItemId attribute
		 of a <Site> element.
		An optional position parameter specifies the index at
		 which the site should be created in its direct parent.

methods.name: addMenuItem
methods.desc:
Adds a new menu item to a given menu. 
		 
		The menu argument 
		 can be a Menu Constant or id 
		 indicating the area of user interface where you want to add the 
		 menu item.
		The caption 
		 argument specifies a default label for the menu item.
		The position parameter specifies where 
		 the menu item will be added in the given menu. 
		 Any value less than zero is indexed from the end of the menu. 
		 By default, a new menu item is appended to the end of a menu. 
		 
		The command 
		 argument specifies a command by name that is executed when you 
		 interact with the menu item. For example, you can pass the name 
		 of a command registered to the application or an id that can be 
		 referenced when adding gallery menu items.
		The tool_tip 
		 argument specifies a default tooltip for the menu item.
		The image argument 
		 specifies the icon of the menu item.
		The reference_id 
		 argument refers to another menu item by its command name or id. 
		 Generally, you would use this to add items to a gallery menu on 
		 the Ribbon in which both the gallery and its items are created 
		 using the same Python command.
		The control_type 
		 argument specifies the control type of the menu item. Generally, 
		 you would use this to indicate an item as a GalleryMenuTool 
		 or GalleryMenuToolItem. If you are creating 
		 a contextual tab group in the Ribbon, you would use this to indicate 
		 a ContextualTabGroup or RibbonTab.
		Each call returns an integer that is a handle 
		 for the new menu item. Use that value in the removeMenuItem() 
		 method to delete the menu item.
		See Creating 
		 a Python Add-on for more information and examples.

methods.name: createBehaviourMenuItem
methods.desc:
Creates a new menu item in Behavior tab add-on menu. 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use addMenuItem() method.

methods.name: createFeatureMenuItem
methods.desc:
Creates a new menu item in Geometry tab add-on menu. 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use addMenuItem() method.

methods.name: createGeometryMenuItem
methods.desc:
Creates a new menu item in Geometry tab add-on menu. 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use addMenuItem() method.

methods.name: createMenuItem
methods.desc:
Creates a new menu item in Add-ons menu. 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use addMenuItem() method.

methods.name: getLocalizedString
methods.desc:
Gets the value of a given key in a resource file based on the 
		 language of the application. 
		Generally, this is used to localize add-ons. 
		 If the key is not found, returns the key itself as a string.
		You have two options:
		1-key
		Pass the entire key, for example "ComboKey::Python.MsgBoxTitle.Text".
		3-key
		Pass the key in three separate arguments, for example ("Python","MsgBoxTitle","Text").
		See Template 
		 for Python Add-on for an example on how to use this method.

methods.name: removeMenuItem
methods.desc:
Remove a menu item that was previously added using the addMenuItem() 
		 method.

methods.name: setContextualTabGroup
methods.desc:
Turns on/off the visibility of a contextual tab group in Ribbon. 
		 
		The tab_id argument 
		 refers to the Id of the contextual tab group.

methods.name: getSelection
methods.desc:
Returns a selection object for a given type. 
		 
		See Selection 
		 constants for available types.
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use vcSelectionManager.

methods.name: getSelections
methods.desc:
Returns a list of selection objects for all types registered 
		 to the application. 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use vcSelectionManager.

methods.name: delayRealTime
methods.desc:
Executes a delay (in seconds) that 
		 halts a running simulation.

methods.name: getSimulation
methods.desc: Returns the simulation object of application.

methods.name: resetSimulation
methods.desc:
Resets the simulation to its initial state. 
		Resetting a simulation removes all dynamic 
		 components and returns static components to their initial state 
		 at the start of a simulation.

methods.name: startSimulation
methods.desc:
Starts a simulation. 
		An optional stop_time 
		 argument can be given to indicate when to stop running the simulation.
		If the simulation of the application is 
		 not at its initial state, the simulation will continue from its 
		 current state. That is, the simulation clock will not reset to 
		 zero.

methods.name: stopSimulation
methods.desc: Immediately stops the execution of a simulation.

methods.name: createQuantity
methods.desc:
Create a new quantity of a given name 
		 and type. 
		The name argument 
		 specifies the full name of the new quantity. The type 
		 argument specifies whether a scalar or vector quantity.
		See Quantity 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: createUnitFamily
methods.desc:
Create a new unit family of a given name 
		 in application. 
		The name argument 
		 specifies the name of the unit family and may not contain dot 
		 characters.

methods.name: createUnitGroup
methods.desc:
Create a new unit group of a given name. 
		 
		The name argument 
		 specifies the name of the unit group and may not contain dot characters.

methods.name: deleteUnitFamily
methods.desc:
Deletes a unit family given as an argument. 
		Only user-created unit families can be deleted.

methods.name: deleteUnitGroup
methods.desc:
Deletes a unit group given as an argument. 
		Only user-created unit groups can be deleted.

methods.name: findQuantity
methods.desc:
Returns a quantity matching a given name; 
		 otherwise returns None.

methods.name: findUnit
methods.desc:
Returns a unit matching a given name; 
		 otherwise returns None. 
		This method will try to match either the 
		 name or suffix of a unit to the given name.

methods.name: findUnitFamily
methods.desc:
Returns a unit family matching a given name; 
		 otherwise returns None.

methods.name: findUnitGroup
methods.desc:
Returns a unit group matching a given name; 
		 otherwise returns None.

methods.name: createView
methods.desc:
Creates a new view of a given name 
		 based on the current 3D world view. 
		The view itself is saved with a layout and 
		 listed as a User View in the GUI whenever the layout is loaded 
		 in the 3D world.

methods.name: deleteView
methods.desc:
Deletes a view matching a given name 
		 from the current layout.

methods.name: findView
methods.desc:
Returns a view matching a given name 
		 in the current layout; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: setClipPlane
methods.desc: Sets the clipping plane position.

methods.name: setClipPlaneEnabled
methods.desc: Defines if the clipping plane is enabled or disabled.

methods.name: useView
methods.desc:
Switches the view of the 3D world to a view matching a given 
		 name in the current layout. 
		An optional time 
		 argument can be given to interpolate the linear movement of the 
		 camera to new view. That is, a timed camera movement (in seconds).

methods.name: autoShareFeatureTrees
methods.desc:
Shares the feature trees of identical components in 3D world. 
		 
		For example, exact copies of a conveyor 
		 with the same VCID and feature trees can be shared to consume 
		 less memory.
		If you need to make a vcComponent 
		 object unique again, edit a property that affects one of its features 
		 or call its makeUnique() method.

methods.name: clearMessages
methods.desc: Clears Output panel.

methods.name: clearUndo
methods.desc: Clears the undo history.

methods.name: detectFrameOwnerNode
methods.desc:
Returns a node containing the closest Frame feature to a given 
		 position based on a distance tolerance. 
		An optional exclude 
		 argument can be given to exclude frames belonging to specific 
		 node.

methods.name: getApplicationPath
methods.desc:
Returns the Uri of this application's script as a formatted 
		 string. 
		Generally, this method is used to register 
		 a command used in a Python add-on.

methods.name: getPythonDllPath
methods.desc: Returns the Uri of Python DLL folder as a formatted string.

methods.name: getRandomSeed
methods.desc: Returns the integer of a random generator at a given index.

methods.name: getMessages
methods.desc: Returns all messages currently listed in the Output panel.

methods.name: messageBox
methods.desc:
Shows a message box displaying the given message. 
		 
		An optional title 
		 argument can be given to define the title of the message box.
		An optional type 
		 argument can given to define the box type and icon.
		An optional buttons 
		 argument can be given to show a message box with buttons.
		The method returns a result based on the 
		 type of message box and which button is clicked by a user.
		See Message 
		 Constants for more information.
		See Example 
		 on how to implement this method.
		Warning: If 
		 you want to open a message box when you start the application, 
		 you should use the OnAppInitialized event to verify it is safe 
		 to generate the box.

methods.name: rayCast
methods.desc:
Tests if a ray with a given ray_length and start_position 
		 intersects an object in the current layout. 
		The position of the ray is based in the 
		 World coordinate system, and the length of the ray is directed 
		 along the positive Z-axis.
		An optional exclude_node 
		 argument can be given to exclude a node, thereby allowing the 
		 ray to cast through and ignore collision with the given node and 
		 its child nodes.
		An optional use_backface 
		 argument has a default True value to include geometry backfaces 
		 in ray casting. A False value means the ray ignores geometry backfaces.
		An optional tuple argument of node, 
		 inclusion_type and inclusion scope can be given 
		 to exclude or include nodes. Excluding nodes allows the ray to 
		 cast through and ignore collision with the given nodes. Including 
		 one or more nodes will automatically exclude all the other nodes 
		 not included.
		See Collision 
		 Detector Constants for more information.
		If a ray collides with an object, the collision 
		 data is returned as tuple with three or five elements; otherwise 
		 returns None.
		See Example 
		 on how to implement this method.

methods.name: render
methods.desc: Renders the scene of 3D world.

methods.name: save
methods.desc:
Saves the contents of 3D world as a layout using a given uri. Also includecomponents 
		 parameter defines if the components are included in the layout.

properties.name: ActivationKey
properties.desc:
Gets the floating or stand-alone license that is currently 
		 used for the licensing of the application.

properties.name: AuthorContext
properties.desc: Gets the Modeling tab context.

properties.name: Commands
properties.desc:
Gets a list of commands in the application's command registry. 
		 That is, registered commands available in the application.

properties.name: Components
properties.desc: Gets a list of all components in the 3D world.

properties.name: ConfigureContext
properties.desc: Gets the Home tab context.

properties.name: Contexts
properties.desc: Gets a list of all contexts defined in the application.

properties.name: CurrentContext
properties.desc: Defines the current context of the application.

properties.name: CustomProductVersion
properties.desc:
Returns the config file customized product version. If the 
		 product name has not been customized, returns the internal version.

properties.name: CurrentSelection
properties.desc:
Defines the current selection in the active environment. 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use selection type methods or the SelectionManager property.

properties.name: Dashboard
properties.desc: Gets the Statistics dashboard.

properties.name: DrawingContext
properties.desc: Gets the Drawing tab context.

properties.name: IgnoreEvents
properties.desc:
Defines if the application ignores events. 
		Generally, a True value is used in situations 
		 where events could create cyclic calls and unintentional loops.

properties.name: Layers
properties.desc: Gets a list of all layers in the current layout.

properties.name: LayoutItems
properties.desc: Gets a list of all layout items in the current layout.

properties.name: LayoutModified
properties.desc:
Defines if the current layout has been modified since it was 
		 loaded or its last save. 
		LayoutModified acts as a flag for determining 
		 if you are prompted to save a layout and the current state of 
		 the Save command.
		The value is set to True when a user makes 
		 a change to the current layout using the GUI.
		A script that makes changes to a layout 
		 should set the value to True in order for the application to know 
		 whether or not the layout needs to be saved. This is not needed 
		 if the script only makes temporary changes to a layout during 
		 a simulation.

properties.name: LayoutPath
properties.desc:
Gets the local path of current layout. 
		Generally, the path is the same one you 
		 would get from the address bar of the File Explorer in Windows. 
		 For example, spaces would not be encoded as + signs.
		See System.Uri.LocalPath 
		 in the .NET Framework for more information.

properties.name: LayoutUri
properties.desc:
Gets the URI of current layout. 
		The URI would contain its scheme, for example 
		 a "file:///" prefix, and spaces would be encoded as 
		 + signs.
		See Example. Print 
		 URI of current layout for more information.

properties.name: LayoutUriInCompatibilityFormat
properties.desc:
Gets the URI of current layout in a format that was used in 
		 older product versions. 
		The URI is similar to LayoutUri. One exception 
		 is a forward slash in the URI path is replaced with a backslash.

properties.name: Lights
properties.desc: Gets a list of all lights in the application.

properties.name: Materials
properties.desc: Gets a list of all materials in the application.

properties.name: PdfFileName
properties.desc:
Defines the filename for a recorded 3D PDF. 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use the RecordingFileName property.

properties.name: PdfRecord
properties.desc:
Defines if a simulation is recorded as a 3D PDF. 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use the Recording property.

properties.name: PdfShow
properties.desc:
Defines if the created 3D PDF is opened after recording a simulation. 
		 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use the RecordingShow property.

properties.name: PdfStepSize
properties.desc:
Defines the keyframe rate for recording simulations as 3D PDF. 
		 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use the RecordingFrameRate property.

properties.name: ProcessContext
properties.desc: Gets the Process tab context.

properties.name: ProductClass
properties.desc:
Gets the name of the application's product class. 
		Product classes are Creator, Configurator 
		 and Viewer.

properties.name: ProductKey
properties.desc: Gets the latest stand-alone key used to activate the application.

properties.name: ProductName
properties.desc: Gets the product name of the application.

properties.name: ProductVersion
properties.desc:
Gets the product version of the application. 
		The product version format is the major 
		 version number, minor version number and the revision number in 
		 that order separated by periods.

properties.name: ProgressStatus
properties.desc:
Defines the product status message given when the ProgressValue 
		 property is set to True. 
		Caution: ProgressValue 
		 must always be set after setting ProgressStatus. Failure to do 
		 so may cause the application's GUI to enter an indefinite locked 
		 state.

properties.name: ProgressValue
properties.desc:
Defines the current state of the application's progress bar. 
		 
		Value < 0.0
		Progress is unknown or stalled. Setting this value will lock the 
		 GUI and activate the progress bar.
		0.0 <= Value <= 
		 1.0
		The current state of progress is within this range in which 0.0 
		 indicates no progress and 1.0 indicates full progress. Setting 
		 this value will lock the GUI and activate progress bar.
		Value > 1.0
		The operation has been completed. Setting this value will unlock 
		 the GUI and deactivate the progress bar.
		Caution: If 
		 ProgressValue is used to indicate the status of an operation, 
		 the set value must always be greater than 1.0 after completing 
		 the operation to unlock the application's GUI. Otherwise, the 
		 GUI may enter an indefinite locked state.

properties.name: PythonActionPanel
properties.desc: The action panel can be opened when executing a python command

properties.name: Quantities
properties.desc: Gets a list of all scalar quantities in the application.

properties.name: RealTime
properties.desc: Gets the current computer time (in seconds).

properties.name: RealTimeMode
properties.desc:
Defines if a simulation runs in real time or virtual time. 
		 
		A True value means the simulation runs at 
		 a speed indicative of the real world environment. A False value 
		 means the simulations runs at speed based on the device's CPU 
		 processing speed.

properties.name: Recorder
properties.desc:
Defines if a simulation is recorded as a 3D PDF or video. 
		See Recording 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: Recording
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the recording of a simulation. 
		A True value will start a simulation (if 
		 it was not already running) and the recording, whereas a False 
		 value will stop a simulation and the recording.
		Note: A recording 
		 cannot be stopped and continued without generating a new file.

properties.name: RecordingFileName
properties.desc: Defines the absolute path of a recorded simulation file.

properties.name: RecordingFrameRate
properties.desc: Defines the frame rate for recording simulations.

properties.name: RecordingHeight
properties.desc:
Defines the height (number of pixels) for a simulation recorded 
		 as a video.

properties.name: RecordingShow
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the opening of the recorded simulation file after 
		 recording is stopped in the 3D world.

properties.name: RecordingWidth
properties.desc:
Defines the width (number of pixels) for a simulation recorded 
		 as a video.

properties.name: RecordScreen
properties.desc:
Defines if the size of the 3D world viewport defines the dimensions 
		 of a simulation recorded as a video. 
		A False value means the values of the RecordingHeight 
		 and RecordingWidth properties define the dimensions of a recorded 
		 video.

properties.name: RenderShadows
properties.desc:
Defines the mode for rendering shadows in the 3D world. 
		See Render 
		 Shadows Constants for more information.

properties.name: ResetSimulationAtLoading
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the automatic reset of a component to its initial 
		 state when a new component is added to the 3D world. 
		The default value is True. Generally, a 
		 False value is used in cases where you want to retain the current 
		 joint configuration of robots in the 3D world when teaching positions.
		The effect is the same as executing the 
		 Reset button on the simulation controls.

properties.name: SelectionManager
properties.desc:
Gets the selection manager of the application which is used 
		 for handling selections in an environment.

properties.name: Selections
properties.desc:
Gets a list of selection type objects registered with the application. 
		 That is, the types of objects you can select in an environment 
		 such as the 3D world. 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use vcSelectionManager.

properties.name: Simulation
properties.desc:
Gets the simulation object of the application. 
		Generally, the simulation object is used 
		 to control the execution of a simulation in the 3D world.

properties.name: TeachContext
properties.desc: Gets the Program tab context.

properties.name: UnitFamilies
properties.desc: Gets a list of all unit families in the application.

properties.name: UnitGroups
properties.desc: Gets a list of all unit groups in the application.

properties.name: Views

properties.name: SimulationWorld
properties.desc: Gets the simulation world root node.

properties.name: Workflow
properties.desc: Gets the Workflow.

methods.name: canBeAddedTo
methods.desc:
Returns boolean if child step can be added as a child 
		 to theparent step. 
		  
		If the relation already exists, returns False.

methods.name: canBeMovedTo
methods.desc:
Returns boolean if child step can be moved to be a child 
		 of the parent step at a specified index. 
		  
		If index is outside the range of existing 
		 steps, the method checks if the step can be appended to existing 
		 steps of the parent. 
		  
		If child is already at the requested location 
		 within children of parent, returns False.

methods.name: moveStepTo
methods.desc:
Moves stepToMove and adds it as a child to parent 
		 at specified index. If index is outside the range 
		 of existing steps, the moved step is appended to existing steps 
		 of the parent.

methods.name: cloneStepFrom
methods.desc:
Creates a copy of stepToClone and adds it as a child 
		 to parent at specified index. If index is 
		 outside the range of existing steps, the created copy is appended 
		 to existing steps of the parent. 
		  
		If successful, returns the cloned step.

methods.name: createStepTo
methods.desc:
Create 
		 a new assembly step and adds it as a child to parent at 
		 specified index. If index is outside the 
		 range of existing steps, the created step is appended to existing 
		 steps of the parent.
		If 
		 successful, returns the created step.

properties.name: IPOMode
properties.desc:
Defines the interpolation mode of the frame and the external 
		 configuration of a referencing robot controller. 
		0
		Default setting, so no effect on robot's external configuration.
		1
		Robot position inherits orientation of base frame.
		2
		Robot position inherits orientation of tool frame.
		Interpolation 
		 constants can be used with this property.
		Note: A conflict 
		 can occur if a base-tool pair in a referencing robot have the 
		 same IPOMode property value or cannot be used with the robot's 
		 current configuration.

properties.name: Name

properties.name: Node

properties.name: PositionMatrix
properties.desc:
Defines the frame's position and orientation in the Node property's 
		 coordinate system. 
		The position matrix is a result of the node's 
		 offset, pivot and joint expressions but can be set manually.

properties.name: PositionExpression

		 to avoid passing the event to a user-defined function.

methods.name: addPort
methods.desc:
Connects a port at a given index to a given signal. 
		The port index starts from 0. The PortCount 
		 property should have enough ports. In other words, to add a boolean 
		 signal to port 3 the PortCount value should be at least 4 (ports 
		 0-3), otherwise calling this method will return an error.

methods.name: connect
methods.desc:
Creates a remote connection with another signal map or signal. 
		 
		If a port is connected to a signal, refer 
		 to the abstract interface of the connection to disconnect only 
		 that signal. Otherwise, the disconnect() method will disconnect 
		 all signals connected to the port.
		Signals in components can act as abstract 
		 interfaces between ports, sending and receiving information via 
		 signal maps.   
		 
		See vcBoolSignal 
		 for more information.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.desc:
Disconnects a port at a given index 
		 from its connections.

methods.name: getAllConnectedPorts
methods.desc: Returns a list of all connected ports in the signal map.

methods.name: getPortName
methods.desc:
Returns the name of a port at a given index. 
		 
		Note: If the 
		 port has no signal then its name is an empty string.

methods.name: getInternalPortSignal
methods.desc:
Returns the signal connected to a port at given 
		 index; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: getConnectedExternalSignals
methods.desc:
Returns a list of all signals in other components connected 
		 to a local port at the given index in the signal map; otherwise 
		 returns an empty list.

methods.name: getConnectedExternalPorts
methods.desc:
Returns a list of all ports in other components connected to 
		 a local port at a given index in the signal map; otherwise returns 
		 an empty list.

methods.name: input
methods.desc: Returns the value of a port at a given index.

methods.name: output

Sets the value of a port at a given index 
		 to a given value.

methods.name: setPortName
methods.desc:
Sets the name of a port at a given index 
		 to a given name. 
		Note: The port 
		 must have a signal in order to be assigned a name.

methods.name: setPortSignal
methods.desc:
Sets the signal of a port at a given index. 
		 
		An optional signal 
		 argument can be given to assign the port a signal in its component. 
		 Otherwise, the port is assigned a dynamic, application signal.

methods.name: trySetDirection
methods.desc:
Tries to set a direction for 
		 the Boolean Signal Map. 
		
		If setting the direction was successful, returns True. Otherwise, 
		 returns False.

properties.name: Listeners
properties.desc: Defines a list of behaviors using the signal map.

properties.name: Direction
properties.desc:
Defines the direction of ports in the signal map. Ports can 
		 be set as inputs, outputs or undefined. If ports are defined as 
		 inputs, they cannot be used as outputs or vice versa. To set the 
		 direction it is recommended to use the trySetDirection 
		 Method instead.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of the signal map.

properties.name: StartIndex
properties.desc:
Defines the start index of ports in the signal map. It can 
		 be used in conjunction with EndIndex to define the amount of ports in 
		 the signal map.

properties.name: EndIndex
properties.desc:
Defines the end index of ports in the signal map. Its value 
		 is updated automatically when setting Ports or PortCount.

properties.name: PortCount
properties.desc: Same as Ports, defines the number of ports in map.

properties.name: Ports
properties.desc:
Same as PortCount, defines the number of ports in the signal 
		 map.

methods.name: signal
methods.desc:
Signals the current value of signal to all connected behaviors, 
		 thereby triggering the OnSignal event. 
		An optional value 
		 argument can be given to set the Value property of the signal.

properties.name: Value
properties.desc:
Defines the value of signal. 
		Setting this value does not trigger the 
		 OnSignal event unless you use the signal() method.

methods.name: getRay
methods.desc: Gets the ray based on the image coordinate system.

properties.name: ClipFar
properties.desc:
Defines how far objects can be from a camera in order to be 
		 displayed. If objects are too far then they are not visible.

properties.name: ClippingMethod
properties.desc:
Defines the clipping mode for a camera's view. 
		Clipping is used to determine how close 
		 and far objects can be from a camera to be displayed on screen.
		
		0 = VC_RENDER_CLIPPING_AUTOMATIC
		1 = VC_RENDER_CLIPPING_CLASSIC
		2 = VC_RENDER_CLIPPING_MANUAL
		Classic 
		 is the default setting for the application. Automatic 
		 tries to keep all objects in view of a camera visible. Manual 
		 allows a user to specify the near and far distances for clipping.
		Manual mode uses ClipNear 
		 and ClipFar properties 
		 to define a clip-volume space of a camera's projected view. Objects 
		 within the area defined by ClipNear and ClipFar are displayed 
		 based on a camera's center of interest and eye settings.
		Example. Clipping 
		 a camera's perspective view
		
		Clipping can be defined manually in orthographic 
		 view when needed; otherwise, Classic mode is recommended.

properties.name: ClipNear
properties.desc:
Defines how close objects can be to a camera in order to be 
		 displayed. If objects are too close then they are not visible.

properties.name: Coi
properties.desc: Defines camera's center of interest location.

properties.name: Eye
properties.desc: Defines camera's eye location.

properties.name: Matrix
properties.desc: Defines the whole camera matrix.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of the camera.

properties.name: NavigationDisabled
properties.desc:
Defines if navigation commands in GUI are turned on or off 
		 to allow camera orientation with other tools.

properties.name: CaseCondition
properties.desc:
Gets or sets an expression which will 
		 be evaluated against statement's Condition.
