methods.desc:
Returns true if any collision between NodeListA and a bound 
		 box defined by given corner points. 
		An optional transformation 
		 argument can be given to transform the bound box using World coordinates.
		If no tolerance 
		 is given, test uses zero distance.

methods.name: testAllCollisions
methods.desc:
Returns true if any collision between NodeListA and NodeListB. 
		 
		If no tolerance 
		 is given, test uses zero distance.

methods.name: testBBoxComponentCollisions
methods.desc:
Returns true if a component collides with a bound box defined 
		 by given corner points. 
		An optional bbox_reference 
		 argument can be given to transform the bound box using 
		 World coordinates.

methods.name: testBBoxNodeCollisions
methods.desc:
Returns true if a node collides with a bound box defined by 
		 given corner points. 
		An optional bbox_reference 
		 argument can be given to transform the bound box using 
		 World coordinates.

methods.name: testComponentCollisions
methods.desc: Returns true if collision detected with component.

methods.name: testMinimumDistance
methods.desc:
Returns true if collision detected with a given tolerance 
		 value.

methods.name: testNodeCollisions
methods.desc: Returns true if collision detected with node.

methods.name: testOneBBoxCollision
methods.desc:
Returns true for first collision between NodeListA and a bound 
		 box defined by given corner points. 
		An optional transformation 
		 argument can be given to transform the bound box using World coordinates.
		If no tolerance 
		 is given, test uses zero distance.

methods.name: testOneCollision
methods.desc:
Returns true for first collision between NodeListA and NodeListB. 
		 
		If no tolerance 
		 is given, test uses zero distance.

properties.name: Active
properties.desc: Turns on/off the use of collision test.

properties.name: CollisionMaterial
properties.desc: Get/Set material of the collided node.

properties.name: DisplayMinimumDistance
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the display of minimum distance in the 3D world 
		 between objects in a collision test that uses a distance tolerance 
		 greater than zero.

properties.name: FirstCollision
properties.desc:
Defines if collision test only records the first detected collision. 
		 
		A True value records the first collision. 
		 A False value records all collisions.
		FirstCollision is automatically disabled 
		 when the Tolerance property has a value greater than zero. This 
		 is done in order to calculate the minimum distance between two 
		 objects based on all detected collisions in the test.

properties.name: HitCount
properties.desc: Gets the number of detected collisions.

properties.name: IgnoreClosestNodes
properties.desc:
Ignores collisions between two nodes if a node is either parent 
		 or child to the other node. This can be used to test self-collision 
		 of a component. Default value is False.

properties.name: IgnoreDifferentComponents
properties.desc:
Ignores collisions between nodes when they are on different 
		 components. This can be used to test multiple self-collisions 
		 of components. Default value is False.

properties.name: NodeBCollisionMaterial
properties.desc:
Get/Set material of the collided node B. This property will 
		 define the node B material over CollisionMaterial.

properties.name: NodeListA
properties.desc:
Defines a list of nodes to compare with NodeListB. 
		See Collision 
		 Detector Constants for more information.

properties.name: NodeListB
properties.desc:
Defines a list of nodes to compare with NodeListA. 
		See Collision 
		 Detector Constants for more information.

properties.name: StopOnCollision
properties.desc:
Defines if a simulation is stopped when there is a detected 
		 collision.

properties.name: Tolerance
properties.desc:
Defines a distance tolerance for detecting collisions before 
		 objects in the test collide with one another. 
		 
		Note that if Tolerance is set to zero, a simplified 
		 collision detection algorithm is used. This algorithm does not 
		 detect collisions if one geometry is completely enclosed by the 
		 other, so for example, if the bounding box surfaces do not intersect.

methods.name: addState
methods.desc:
Adds a command state function to Python command. 
		The first added command state is the function 
		 called when command is executed.
		This method is only available for user-defined Python commands.

methods.name: cancelNextClick
methods.desc:
Cancels a next click event. 
		This prevents a mouse click from being detected 
		 during the next mouse up event. This is only useful when called 
		 from an event processing handler function. Generally, this is 
		 used to prevent the activation of the Select command in response 
		 to a mouse click. 
		This method is only available for user-defined Python commands 
		 and can only be called from within the command script itself.

methods.name: createProperty
methods.desc:
Adds a new property of a given type 
		 and name to command object. 
		An optional constraints argument can be 
		 used to define constraints for property, which must be done at 
		 time of creation.
		See Property 
		 Constants for more information.
		This method is only available for user-defined 
		 Python commands.

methods.name: deleteProperty
methods.desc:
Removes a given property or one 
		 matching a given name from command. 
		 
		This method is only available for user-defined 
		 Python commands.

methods.name: execute
methods.desc:
Executes the command, and then waits for the execution of first 
		 command state to be completed. 
		  
		If this method is called with no arguments, the 
		 arguments used are those currently set in the command object. 
		 
		  
		If this method is called with positional arguments, 
		 each value is assigned to command properties in the order they 
		 were created before command execution. 
		  
		If the method is called with keyword arguments, 
		 the corresponding command parameter property is looked up and 
		 assigned the argument value. If a parameter cannot be found, the 
		 function fails.

methods.name: executeAsTool
methods.desc:
Executes the command as if its execution type is VC_COMMAND_TOOL. 
		 
		This method overrides the command's ExecutionType 
		 property.

methods.name: executeInActionPanel
methods.desc:
Executes a command using a task pane. 
		Generally, you would use a task pane to 
		 display the options of a registered Python or .NET command and 
		 to further control its execution.
		For more information, see Command 
		 Task Pane in Creating a Python Add-on topic.

methods.name: getApplication
methods.desc: Returns the application object.

methods.name: getCommand
methods.desc: Returns the command object.

methods.name: getCommandPath
methods.desc:
Returns the URI used by application to load the Python file 
		 of command. 
		This method returns an empty string if the 
		 command is not a Python command.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc:
Returns a property matching a given name 
		 in command; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: getSimulation
methods.desc: Returns the simulation object.

methods.name: genVarSpaceDialog
methods.desc:
Shows a modal property dialog containing the properties of 
		 a registered command matching a given command_name. 
		 
		Note: The command_name is specific to 
		 Python, so COM or other programming commands cannot be used as 
		 an argument.
		The title of the dialog window is set to 
		 dialog_title. The first_tab_caption parameter 
		 determines whether a tabbed dialog is used. If first_tab_caption 
		 is an empty string, the properties are displayed in a single pane. 
		 Otherwise, the properties are displayed in separate tabs. In that 
		 case, property names are parsed as "tabName::propertyName" 
		 and distributed into tabs according to tabName; and properties 
		 without a double colon "::" in the name are displayed 
		 in the first tab, which will have the caption set to first_tab_caption.
		After the command is executed, the Param_4 
		 property of the command object contains the result of the dialog, 
		 as an integer. A value of 1 means a user clicked OK, whereas a 
		 value of 2 means a user clicked Cancel.

methods.name: recompile
methods.desc: Recompiles the command.

methods.name: setEventState
methods.desc:
Enters event processing mode. This method also sets event state 
		 handler function, where interactive events can be processed. 
		The event handler function is called with 
		 one parameter, which is of type vcCommandEvent. 
		 The only way to leave event processing mode is to call setNextState() 
		 method.
		This method is only available with Python 
		 commands, and can only be called from within the command script 
		 itself.

methods.name: setNextState
methods.desc:
Sets the next command state function. 
		 This is a function which is called with no parameters in order 
		 to execute the next state. If None is passed as a parameter, the 
		 command will exit after the current state function or event processing 
		 function returns. 
		Calling this method will also cause the 
		 command to leave event processing mode.
		This method is only available in Python 
		 commands, and can only be called from within the command script 
		 itself.

properties.name: Application
properties.desc: Gets the application object.

properties.name: Checked
properties.desc:
Defines if command is checked or visually indicated as active 
		 in the GUI, which is only for Python commands.

properties.name: Enabled
properties.desc:
Defines if command is enabled/disabled, which is only for Python 
		 commands. 
		A False value means the command will be 
		 greyed out in the GUI.

properties.name: ExecutionType
properties.desc:
Defines how other active commands are managed when executing 
		 this command. 
		See Command 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: Icon
properties.desc: Defines the icon of command in the GUI.

properties.name: IgnoreEvents
properties.desc:
Defines if event passing is ignored when executing command. 
		 
		This flag is used in situations where events 
		 could create cyclic calls.

properties.name: IsActive
properties.desc:
Gets the current state of command. 
		A True value means the command is active.

properties.name: IsModelingCommand
properties.desc:
Defines if command is used for manipulating geometry and related 
		 properties.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of command.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc:
Gets a list containing all properties of command. 
		Generally, properties are used to pass information 
		 to and from the command implementation for execution.

properties.name: Simulation
properties.desc: Gets the simulation object.

properties.name: SupportsOverrideActivation
properties.desc:
Defines if command is restarted after the execution of an override 
		 command, which is only for Python commands.

properties.name: EyeToMouse
properties.desc:
Gets offset (in World coordinates) from the camera eye point 
		 to the pointer on view plane.

properties.name: Key
properties.desc:
Gets either the Windows scan code for a pressed key or an offset 
		 value for a mouse wheel movement in which a negative value indicates 
		 a downward rotation of a mouse wheel.

properties.name: MouseOnFloor
properties.desc:
Gets the position of the mouse on the layout floor (ex: Z == 
		 0) in World coordinates.

properties.name: MouseOnViewPlane
properties.desc:
Gets the position of the pointer on the view plane in World 
		 coordinates.

properties.name: ShiftState
properties.desc:
Gets the bit mask indicating which mouse buttons or modifier 
		 keys are pressed by a user. There are also bits for single and 
		 double click detection. 
		See Command 
		 Event Constants more for information.

properties.name: Type
properties.desc:
Gets the command event type. 
		See Command 
		 Event Constants more for information.

properties.name: X
properties.desc: Gets the X-axis coordinate of pointer in the 3D window.

properties.name: Y
properties.desc: Gets the Y-axis coordinate of pointer in the 3D window.

methods.name: addLine
methods.desc: Creates a new line in set using a list of given points.

methods.name: deleteLine
methods.desc:
Deletes a line at a given index 
		 from set.

methods.name: getLinePointCount
methods.desc:
Returns the number of points in a line at a given index 
		 in set.

methods.name: getLine
methods.desc:
Returns a list of position vectors for each point of a line 
		 at a given index in set.

properties.name: CurveData
properties.desc:
Gets the container of 
		 mathematical information used for rendering curves.

properties.name: Lines
properties.desc:
Gets a list of lines where each line is a list of position 
		 vectors for its points.

properties.name: LineCount
properties.desc: Gets the total number of lines in the set.

properties.name: LineWidth
properties.desc: Defines the width of each line in the set.

methods.name: clone
methods.desc:
Creates a clone of component in 3D world, and then returns 
		 the new component. 
		If shared 
		 argument is non-zero the clone and original share geometry. That 
		 is, feature tree is shared not copied. This improves performance 
		 during simulation, but the cloned components cannot be edited 
		 separately (changing the appearance of either clone or original 
		 component affects all the others.)
		Cloning of a component is not allowed when 
		 1) it's not attached to World 2) there is a hierarchy lock in 
		 the node tree, which happens during layout loading, or while moving 
		 a node from one place to another.

methods.name: createProperty
methods.desc:
Adds a new property of a given type 
		 and name to component, and then returns 
		 the new property. 
		An optional constraints 
		 argument can be used to define constraints for new property, which 
		 must be defined at the time of creation.
		See Property Constants 
		 for more information.

methods.name: deleteProperty
methods.desc:
Deletes a given property 
		 from component.

methods.name: getPathDistance
methods.desc:
If component is on a path, for example a conveyor path, returns 
		 the distance of component on path.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc:
Returns a property matching a given name 
		 in component; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: getTransportInfo
methods.desc:
Returns information about a transport action for a given component. 
		 
		Generally, a transport action is defined 
		 using an Action Container, Python Script and Transport Protocol.
		See Transportation 
		 Constants for information on availability 
		 options.

methods.name: incrementRevision
methods.desc:
Increments the revision number of a file when using the save() 
		 method. 
		The effect is the same as the Increment 
		 Revision property in the Credits dialog when saving a file.

methods.name: makeUnique
methods.desc:
Makes the feature trees of the component unique, thereby they 
		 are not shared with other components.

methods.name: save
methods.desc:
Saves component to file using a given uri. 
		 
		To save the component with a new VCID, set 
		 the VCID property of the component to an empty string.

methods.name: saveState
methods.desc: Saves the current state of component as its initial state.

methods.name: startMovement
methods.desc:
Start the movement of component in a flow, for example a path. 
		 
		An optional Boolean argument can be used 
		 to override flow logic, thereby forcing component to move in flow.

methods.name: stopMovement
methods.desc:
Stops the movement of component in a flow, for example a path. 
		 
		An optional Boolean argument can be used 
		 to override flow logic, thereby forcing component to not move 
		 in flow.

methods.name: transfer
methods.desc:
Transfers component into a flow and blocks Python execution 
		 until completion of transfer. 
		One option allows you to give two separate 
		 arguments for a behavior and port.
		Another option allows you to give a connector 
		 for performing transfer.
		A given behavior must be or derive from 
		 vcFlow and you should check for available 
		 capacity.

methods.name: transferNonBlocking
methods.desc:
Transfers component into a flow defined by a given behaviour 
		 and port without blocking Python execution. 
		 That is, call is executed immediately and does not wait for completion 
		 of transfer. 
		A given behavior must be or derive from 
		 vcFlow and you should check for available 
		 capacity.

properties.name: BackfaceMode
properties.desc:
Defines the mode for rendering geometry backfaces of component. 
		 That is, geometry not facing active camera. 
		See Component 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: BOM
properties.desc: If a component is included in the bill of materials.

properties.name: BOMdescription
properties.desc: Component description in the bill of materials.

properties.name: BOMname
properties.desc: Component name in the bill of materials.

properties.name: Category
properties.desc: Defines the component group in Cell Graph.

properties.name: Container
properties.desc:
Gets the container storing the component. 
		If a component is not stored in a container, 
		 the value is None.
		Note: Container 
		 refers to a behavior that can store components, for example a 
		 One Way Path.

properties.name: CreationTime
properties.desc:
Defines the creation time of component. 
		Generally, creation time is used for gathering 
		 statistics about components created during a simulation.
		In some cases, you might want to edit the 
		 creation time of a component for filtering, tracking, assembly 
		 and manufacturing purposes.

properties.name: IsUnique
properties.desc:
Indicates if the component is sharing its feature trees with 
		 other components.

properties.name: Locked
properties.desc:
Defines if the component is locked from being edited or manipulated 
		 in 3D world.

properties.name: Material
properties.desc:
Defines the material of component and any of its features which 
		 do not have an assigned material or whose node is set to inherit 
		 a material. 
		This material definition is persistent data, 
		 meaning that the definition is stored when saving component.
		Note: Changing 
		 the material definition of a component causes all geometries to 
		 be rebuilt, which can be a computing intensive operation. For 
		 in-simulation visualization purposes, we recommend using the NodeMaterial 
		 property instead.

properties.name: MovementOrigin
properties.desc: Defines the offset of component when moving on a path.

properties.name: PackFolder
properties.desc: Gets the mechanism for attaching files to component.

properties.name: PathAcceleration
properties.desc: Defines the acceleration of component when moving on a path.

properties.name: PathDeceleration
properties.desc: Defines the deceleration of component when moving on a path.

properties.name: PathVelocity
properties.desc:
Defines the velocity of component when moving on and in the 
		 direction of a path. 
		If a zero value, the velocity of the component 
		 is defined by the path.

properties.name: PDFExportLevel
properties.desc:
Defines the level of detail when exporting component to a 3D 
		 PDF. 
		See Component 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: Product
properties.desc:
The Process Modeling product 
		 instance linked to this component, if any.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc: Gets a list of all user defined properties in component.

properties.name: Uri
properties.desc: Gets the URI of component

properties.name: VCID
properties.desc:
Defines the VCID of component. That is, the unique key identifier 
		 of the component. 
		Generally, you should never set this property. 
		 Instead, allow the application to generate a VCID when you save 
		 the component.

properties.name: Visible
properties.desc: Turns on/off the visibility of component in 3D world.

methods.name: connectInternally
methods.desc:
Connects an internal connector at a given index 
		 in proxy to a given connector.

methods.name: createConnector
methods.desc:
Creates a new connector in proxy. 
		This creates a pair of internal and external 
		 connectors.

methods.name: deleteConnector
methods.desc:
Deletes a connector at a given index 
		 from proxy. 
		This deletes a pair of internal and external 
		 connectors.

methods.name: getInternalConnector
methods.desc:
Returns an internal connector at a given index 
		 in proxy.

methods.name: resetConnectorPort
methods.desc:
Resets a connector at a given index 
		 in proxy, thereby disconnecting the connector from all of its 
		 connections.

properties.name: ComponentSignal
properties.desc:
Defines the signal used for signaling what component has been 
		 transferred into proxy. 
		This property and PortSignal should be used 
		 to determine what and where a component has entered the proxy.

properties.name: DynamicConnections
properties.desc:
Defines if the connectors of proxy are dynamic. That is, connections 
		 will be established during a simulation by using a Python script 
		 or command.

properties.name: InternalConnectorCount
properties.desc:
Gets the number of connectors in proxy. 
		An internal connector is always paired with 
		 an external connector, so this count will match the count for 
		 the proxy's external connectors.

properties.name: PortSignal
properties.desc:
Defines the signal used for signaling which connector a component 
		 used to enter proxy. 
		The value is the index position of the connector 
		 in the proxy's list of connectors.

methods.name: create
methods.desc:
Creates a new component from template, and then returns the 
		 new component. 
		An optional 
		 wait argument can be given to use 
		 BlockingOptimization. If True, the creator waits for capacity 
		 before trying to make a component.
		If creation fails, returns None. Generally, 
		 this occurs when the template is undefined or because of capacity 
		 issues.
		Tip: Set the 
		 Limit property to zero in order to disable the internal logic 
		 of the creator.

properties.name: BlockingOptimization
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the optimization 
		 of creator when making new components, thereby improving simulation 
		 performance. 
		If True, the creator will not check for 
		 capacity rather listen for event. The creator is informed, for 
		 example by component or capacity controller, when there is capacity 
		 to make a new component.

properties.name: Interval
properties.desc: Defines the interval (in seconds) for creating components.

properties.name: Limit
properties.desc:
Defines the maximum number of components that can be created 
		 by creator during a simulation.

properties.name: Part
properties.desc: Defines the URI or VCID of template component.

properties.name: PartPooling
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the reuse of components 
		 made by the creator, thereby improving simulation performance. 
		 
		If True, dynamic components removed during 
		 simulation are recirculated to make new components, thereby reducing 
		 memory allocation.
		Caution: Be 
		 careful when recirculating components that were modified during 
		 simulation, for example a change in node material.

properties.name: TemplateComponent
properties.desc:
Defines the template used by creator to create new components 
		 during a simulation. 
		Either this property or Part can be used 
		 to define the template component of creator.

methods.name: signal
methods.desc:
Signals the current value of signal to all connected behaviors, 
		 thereby triggering the OnSignal event. 
		An optional value 
		 argument can be given to set the Value property of the signal.

properties.name: Value
properties.desc:
Defines the value of signal. 
		Setting this value does not trigger the 
		 OnSignal event unless you use the signal() method.

methods.name: new
methods.desc:
Creates a new vcConfigurableProductTypeFilter object and returns 
		 the new product type filter.

methods.name: bindToStatement
methods.desc:
Adds the filter properties to the given parentObject. 
		 If the filter is already bound, this method first removes the 
		 filter properties from the current parent object, and then adds 
		 the properties to the new parent object.
		
		To remove the filter properties from the current parent object, 
		 set the value of parentObject to None. 
		  
		startingVarGroup defines the vcProperty.Group 
		 value to assign to the first of the properties. The group of the 
		 other properties is based on that value. This defines the order 
		 of the properties in the Visual Components user interface in relation 
		 to the other properties of the parent object. 
		  
		The default of startingVarGroup value 
		 is 10.

properties.name: AcceptAllProductTypesProperty
properties.desc:
Returns True if all product types are accepted.
		
		Returns False if some product types are not accepted.

properties.name: AcceptedFlowGroupsProperty
properties.desc:
Returns the list of flow groups (vcProcessFlowGroup) 
		 that are accepted.

properties.name: AcceptedProductTypesProperty
properties.desc:
Returns the list of product types (vcProductType) 
		 that are accepted.

methods.name: connect
methods.desc:
Connects the connector to a given connector. 
		 
		If no argument is given, this method will 
		 remove all connections of the connector.

methods.name: testCapacity
methods.desc:
Tests the capacity of connector's behavior. 
		Returns True if not at capacity; otherwise 
		 returns False if at full capacity. If the behavior of a connector 
		 does not have physical capacity, for example Component Flow Proxy, 
		 returns None.

methods.name: testConnectedCapacity
methods.desc:
Tests the capacity of behavior connected to the connector. 
		 
		Returns True if not at capacity; otherwise 
		 returns False if at full capacity. If the behavior of a connector 
		 does not have physical capacity, for example Component Flow Proxy, 
		 returns None.

properties.name: Behaviour
properties.desc:
Gets the behavior that the connector is connected to in a component. 
		 
		If no connection, the value is None.

properties.name: CapacityTest
properties.desc:
Define the mode for testing capacity before transferring a 
		 component to an outgoing connection. 
		See Connector 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: Connection
properties.desc:
Defines connector that the connector is connected to in a component. 
		 
		If no connection, the value is None.

properties.name: Index
properties.desc:
Gets the position of the connector in its behavior's list of 
		 connectors.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of connector.

properties.name: Type
properties.desc:
Defines the connector's type. That is, whether the connector 
		 is an Input, Output or Input/Output type port. 
		See Connector 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: Capacity
properties.desc:
Defines the maximum number of components that can be stored 
		 in the container at any given time. That is, the logical capacity 
		 of the container.

properties.name: CapacityBlocks
properties.desc:
Defines a list of Capacity Controller type behaviors that globally 
		 control the capacity of the container. 
		This property overrides the container's 
		 Capacity.

properties.name: ComponentCount
properties.desc: Gets the amount of components stored in the container.

properties.name: Components
properties.desc: Gets a list of components stored in the container.

properties.name: ContentVisible
properties.desc: Sets the visibility of components stored in the container.

properties.name: HeadComponent
properties.desc: Gets a component stored at the head of the container.

properties.name: Statistics
properties.desc:
Defines a Statistics behavior that collects data generated 
		 by the container during a simulation.

properties.name: TailComponent
properties.desc: Gets a component stored at the tail of the container.

properties.name: TransitionSignal
properties.desc:
Defines the signal used for signaling when a component enters/exits 
		 the container. 
		A True value means a component has entered 
		 the container, whereas a False value means a component has exited 
		 the container.

properties.name: Id
properties.desc: Gets the id of the context.

properties.name: clearCurves
properties.desc: Removes all curves from set.

properties.name: createCurveNurbs
properties.access:
Integer degree, List 
		 of vcVector pts
properties.desc:
Adds a new NURBS to set, and then returns the index of curve 
		 in set.

properties.name: createCurvePolyLine
properties.desc:
Adds a new polyline to set, and then returns the index of curve 
		 in set.

properties.name: createCurveSpline
properties.access:
Integer degree, List 
		 of vcVector pts, 
		 List of Integer multiplicities, 
		 List of Real knots, List 
		 of Real weights
properties.desc:
Adds a new spline to set, and then returns the index of curve 
		 in set.

properties.name: deleteCurve
properties.desc:
Deletes a curve at a given index in set. 
		Note: Update 
		 the scene in order to show visualization changes in the 3D world.

properties.name: getCurveEnds
properties.desc:
Returns curve end point information for a curve at a given 
		 index in set. 
		The information defines both curve endpoint 
		 vectors and their weight values, for example if a NURBS curve 
		 is selected.

properties.name: getCurveLength
properties.desc:
Returns the length of a curve at a given index 
		 in set.

properties.name: getCurveMinCurveDistance
properties.desc:
Returns the minimum distance between two curves at given indices 
		 in set. 
		The returned value describes the minimum 
		 distance between curves and minimum distance between either end 
		 points of curves.

properties.name: getCurveMinDistance
properties.desc:
Returns the minimum distance of a curve at a given index 
		 in set to a given point as well as 
		 the length of curve.

properties.name: getCurvePoint
properties.desc:
Returns a point on a curve at a given index 
		 in set and distance from beginning 
		 of curve.

properties.name: getCurvePointAndDerivate
properties.desc:
Returns a point and first derivate vector of a curve at a given 
		 index in set and distance 
		 from beginning of curve.

properties.name: getCurvePointCount
properties.desc: Returns the total number of points for a curve at a given index in set.

properties.name: getCurvePositions
properties.desc:
Returns a list of position matrices for each point on a curve 
		 at a given index in set.

properties.name: getCurveType
properties.desc:
Returns the type of curve at a given index 
		 in set. 
		See Topology 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: getPolyLineCurvePoints
properties.desc:
Returns a list of points for a polyline at a given index 
		 in set; otherwise returns an empty list.

properties.name: getSplineCurveControlPoint
properties.desc:
Returns a list of control points for a spline at a given index in set; otherwise returns an empty 
		 list.

properties.name: getSplineCurveControlWeights
properties.desc:
Returns a list of control weight values for a spline at a given 
		 index in set; otherwise returns an 
		 empty list.

properties.name: getSplineCurveDegree
properties.desc:
Returns the degree of a spline at a given index 
		 in set.

properties.name: getSplineCurveKnots
properties.desc:
Returns spline knot multiplicities (knot recurrence) and knot 
		 values for a curve at a given index 
		 in set.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc: Returns the first property matching a given name in the dimension.

properties.name: ArrowSize
properties.desc: Defines the size of the head and tail arrows of dimension.

properties.name: Dimension
properties.desc: Gets the magnitude (distance in millimeters) of dimension.

properties.name: Height
properties.desc: Defines the height of text in dimension.

properties.name: LineWidth
properties.desc: Defines the line width of dimension.

properties.name: Location
properties.desc: Defines the position matrix of the dimension in World coordinate system.

properties.name: Material
properties.desc: Defines the material of dimension.

properties.name: Node1
properties.desc: Defines the node the head of the dimension is attached to in 3D world.

properties.name: Node2
properties.desc: Defines the node the tail of the dimension is attached to in 3D world.

properties.name: Position1
properties.desc: Defines the position matrix of dimension's head relative to Node1 property's coordinate system.

properties.name: Position2
properties.desc: Defines the position matrix of dimension's tail relative to Node2 property's coordinate system.

properties.name: Thickness
properties.desc: Defines the thickness of text in dimension.

properties.name: Probability
properties.desc:
Defines the weight of the product type, which is used to calculate 
		 the probability for creating product instances of.
		 
		It is evaluated as relative to the sum of all configured probabilities 
		 like a weight value in a weighted sum. The value must be greater 
		 than or equal to zero.

properties.name: ProductType
properties.desc:
Defines the product type of entry to create product instances 
		 of.

properties.name: JointLinkType
properties.desc: Gets the JointType of the link.

properties.name: JointServoType
properties.desc:
Defines whether a joint assigned to a controller is rotational 
		 or translational.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of DOF object and joint.

properties.name: VALUE
properties.desc: Defines the current value of the joint.

properties.name: Direction
properties.desc: Gets a vector from the first point to the second point in edge.

properties.name: Points
properties.desc: Gets a list of two points that define the edge.

properties.name: Polygons
properties.desc: Gets a list of polygons that share the edge.

properties.name: Type
properties.desc:
Gets the edge type. 
		See Edge 
		 Types for more information.

properties.name: Condition
properties.desc:
Defines an expression that when evaluated returns a True or 
		 False value. 
		A True value means the If statement will 
		 execute this scope.
		A False value means the If statement will 
		 not execute this scope.

properties.name: Handled
properties.desc:
Defines if this event has already been handled.
		This is used when an event should only be handled once. All 
		 listeners of the event should begin by checking this value before 
		 performing any operations. If True, then no further operations 
		 should be performed. Otherwise, logic can continue.
		If the listener then handles this event and no further handling 
		 should be done to it, the listener should write True here.

methods.name: callRoutine
methods.desc:
Executes a routine. 
		By default, Python execution is suspended 
		 until the routine has been completed.
		An optional suspendScript 
		 argument can be given a False value, thereby Python execution 
		 continues immediately.
		An optional clearCallStack 
		 argument can be given a False value, thereby the call stack of 
		 executor is not cleared before executing routine.

methods.name: callStatement
methods.desc:
Executes a statement. 
		By default, Python execution is suspended 
		 until the statement has been completed.
		An optional suspendScript 
		 argument can be given a False value, thereby Python execution 
		 continues immediately.
		Note: You can 
		 use callStatement() with a process handler to modify the default 
		 execution of statements in robot program, for example point-to-point 
		 motions, as well as the pre/post execution of statements.

methods.name: setOutput
methods.desc: Sets the value of a signal connected to a port at a given output_index in robot.

methods.name: trySetDigitalInputSignals
methods.desc:
Tries to set the given boolean 
		 signal map behavior as the digital input signals.
		
		If setting the behavior is successful, returns True. Otherwise, 
		 returns False.

methods.name: trySetDigitalOutputSignals
methods.desc:
Tries to set the given boolean 
		 signal map behavior as the digital output signals.
		
		If setting the behavior is successful, returns True. Otherwise, 
		 returns False.

methods.name: waitInput
methods.desc:
Schedules the executor to wait until a signal connected to 
		 a port at a given input_index in robot 
		 has a given value. 
		Note: Python 
		 execution continues immediately.

properties.name: Controller
properties.desc: Defines the controller associated with the executor.

properties.name: CurrentStatement
properties.desc: Gets the statement currently being executed by the executor.

properties.name: DigitalInputSignals
properties.desc: Defines the input signal device associated with the executor.

properties.name: DigitalOutputSignals
properties.desc: Defines the output signal device associated with the executor.

properties.name: IsEnabled
properties.desc: Defines if the program is executed during simulation.

properties.name: IsLooping
properties.desc: Defines if the executor loops its program.

properties.name: ProcessHandlers
properties.desc:
Defines a list of process handlers for overriding or modifying 
		 statements of robot program and executing process statements. 
		 
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use StatementHandler.

properties.name: Program
properties.desc: Gets the program associated with the executor.

properties.name: StatementHandler
properties.desc:
Defines a process handler for controlling the execution of 
		 statements in robot program. 
		See an example of modifying 
		 a point-to-point motion statement.
		Important: Process 
		 statements and Path statements with assigned process handlers 
		 are executed by their handlers. That is, those statements are 
		 not passed on to the statement handler of executor. Do not call 
		 nor try to execute them with the statement handler.

properties.name: UseExternalExecutor
properties.desc:
Defines if the component is controlled by external execution 
		 mechanism, for example a virtual robot controller.

methods.name: attach
methods.desc:
Attaches a given feature to this 
		 feature, thereby allowing you to reorder the containing node's 
		 feature tree. 
		The given feature 
		 cannot be the root feature or parent of this feature.
		An optional rebuild 
		 argument can be used to control the rebuilding of geometry for 
		 an attached feature. Default is False value and will not rebuild 
		 geometry, whereas a True value will rebuild geometry.
		Returns True if attachment is successful; 
		 otherwise returns False.

methods.name: clone
methods.desc:
Copies the feature to the same level in containing node's feature 
		 tree, and then returns the clone.

methods.name: collapse
methods.desc:
Collapses the feature into a new Geometry feature. 
		The original feature will be deleted, thereby 
		 you need to get handle for the new feature.

methods.name: createFeature
methods.desc:
Adds a new feature of a given type 
		 and name as a child of this feature. 
		 
		See Feature 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: createProperty
methods.desc:
Adds a new property of a given type 
		 and name to the feature. 
		An optional constraints 
		 argument can be given to define constraints for the new property, 
		 which must be done at the time of creation.
		See Property 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: delete
methods.desc:
Deletes the feature and its subfeatures, and then returns True; 
		 otherwise returns False.

methods.name: deleteProperty
methods.desc:
Deletes a given property from the 
		 feature.

methods.name: getFeature
methods.desc: Returns the feature.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc: Returns a property of the feature that matches the given name; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: rebuild
methods.desc: Rebuilds the feature and its subfeature tree.

properties.name: Children
properties.desc: Gets a list of feature's immediate child features.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of feature.

properties.name: NodePositionMatrix
properties.desc:
Gets the position matrix of the feature relative to its node's 
		 coordinate system.

properties.name: Parent
properties.desc:
Gets the parent of this feature in the node feature tree. 
		If the feature is root feature, return value 
		 is None.

properties.name: PhysicsCollider
properties.desc: Defines the type of collider used by the feature for physics.

properties.name: PositionMatrix
properties.desc:
Defines the position matrix of this feature relative to its 
		 parent feature's coordinate system.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc: Gets a list of all properties in feature.

properties.name: Type
properties.desc:
Gets the feature type. 
		See Feature 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: Visible
properties.desc: Turns on/off the visibility of the frame in the 3D world.

methods.name: setStep
setGroup
new
methods.desc:
Creates an empty vcFeedOptionFlowInfo object with FlowStep=None, 
		 GroupId="", Group=None

properties.name: FlowStep
properties.desc: Specifies ProcessFlowStep

properties.name: GroupId
properties.desc:
Specifies ProcessGroup's ID inside the FlowStep.
		Alternatively, user can use "" (empty string) to indicate that 
		 any matching ProcessGroup is fine.

properties.name: Group
properties.desc:
Specifies vcProcessGroup object. In case a custom ID is used 
		 for GroupId, this will be None.

properties.name: CapacityAvailable
properties.desc:
Defines if flow object will accept an incoming component. 
		This is not the same as a logical capacity 
		 test since flow type behaviors do not to store components.

properties.name: ConnectorCount
properties.desc: Gets the amount of connectors/ports in flow object.

properties.name: Connectors
properties.desc: Gets a list of connectors in flow object.

properties.name: Statistics
properties.desc:
Defines a Statistics behavior that collects data generated 
		 by this flow during a simulation.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc: Returns a property of the vcStepProcessConfiguration.

properties.name: ProcessGroup
properties.desc: The process groups this configuration is applied to.

properties.name: IsOptional
properties.desc: Defines whether ProcessGroup is optional inside a vcFlowStep.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc: Gets the properties of this vcStepProcessConfiguration.

properties.name: FramePositionMatrix
properties.desc: Gets the position matrix of frame.

properties.name: OriginalFramePositionMatrix
properties.desc: Gets the original position matrix of frame.

methods.name: createFrame
methods.desc: Creates a new frame in set.

methods.name: deleteFrame
methods.desc:
Deletes a frame at a given index 
		 from set.

methods.name: getFrame
methods.desc:
Returns the position matrix of a frame at a given index 
		 in set.

methods.name: setFrame
methods.desc:
Sets the position matrix of a frame at a given index 
		 in set.

methods.name: update
methods.desc:
Updates all frames in set, thereby updating the set's bound 
		 box.

properties.name: FrameCount
properties.desc: Gets the number of frames in set.

properties.name: AxisTextVisible
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the display of axis labels for Frame features 
		 in set. That is, XYZ labels for coordinate axes in a Frame feature. 
		 
		This property is disabled if FramesVisible 
		 is set to False.

properties.name: ConnectingLinesVisible
properties.desc:
Defines if lines are drawn in the 3D world between each Frame 
		 feature in set. 
		The line type is defined by the LineDisplayMode 
		 property.

properties.name: CustomIcon
properties.desc:
Defines the name of a vc3DIcon object 
		 used for rendering each Frame feature in set. 
		Other properties determine if and how a 
		 3D icon is used with the set.

properties.name: FixedSize
properties.desc:
Defines if CustomIcon is scaled to have a constant size relative 
		 to a user's 3D world view. 
		This property is enabled when FrameDisplayMode 
		 is set to use icons and FramesVisible is set to True.

properties.name: FrameDisplayMode
properties.desc:
Defines the mode for rendering Frame features in set. 
		This property is disabled if FramesVisible 
		 is set to False.
		See Frame 
		 Display Mode Constants for more information.

properties.name: FramesVisible
properties.desc: Turns on/off the display of Frame features in set.

properties.name: LineDisplayMode
properties.desc:
Defines the mode for rendering lines between Frame features 
		 in set. 
		This property is disabled if ConnectingLinesVisible 
		 is set to False.
		See Line 
		 Display Mode Constants for more information.

properties.name: LoopLines
properties.desc:
Defines if a line is drawn to connect the first and last Frame 
		 feature in set. 
		This property is disabled if ConnectingLinesVisible 
		 is set to False.

properties.name: Material
properties.desc:
Defines the material of Frame features in set. 
		This might be overridden by the material 
		 of CustomIcon or an individual Frame feature.

properties.name: NamesVisible
properties.desc:
Defines if the name of each Frame feature in set is displayed 
		 in the 3D world. 
		This property is disabled if FramesVisible 
		 is set to False.
		Note: Displaying 
		 the names of Frame features can slow performance and degrade usability 
		 when a large amount of Frame features are contained in a small 
		 area.

methods.name: clear
methods.desc: Removes all geometry sets from container.

methods.name: cloneGeometrySets
methods.desc:
Copies all geometry sets in the container to a given container. 
		 
		An optional offset 
		 argument can be given to offset the copied geometry, thereby making 
		 it easier to distinguish the original from its copy.
		In this case, geometry is shared between 
		 both containers.

methods.name: createGeometrySet
methods.desc:
Creates a new geometry set of a given type 
		 in container. 
		See Geometry 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: deleteGeometrySet
methods.desc:
Deletes a given geometry set or one at a given index 
		 from container.

methods.name: getGeometrySet
methods.desc:
Returns a geometry set at a given index 
		 in container.

methods.name: moveGeometrySets
methods.desc:
Moves all geometry sets in the container to a given container. 
		 
		An optional offset 
		 argument can be given to offset the moved geometry, for example 
		 to apply a node offset.
		In this case, geometry is not shared between 
		 both containers since the original container is now empty.

methods.name: setModified
methods.desc:
Marks the geometry of container as being modified, thereby 
		 alerting the application that changes need to be saved to file.

methods.name: transformContent
methods.desc: Transforms all geometry sets of container by the given matrix.

methods.name: update
methods.desc: Updates the bound box of container.

properties.name: BoundCenter
properties.desc:
Gets a vector from the origin to the center of the container's 
		 bound box.

properties.name: BoundDiagonal
properties.desc:
Gets a half diagonal vector from the center to an upper corner 
		 of the container's bound box using positive axis directions.

properties.name: GeometrySetCount
properties.desc: Gets the amount of geometry sets in container.

properties.name: GeometrySets
properties.desc: Gets a list of geometry sets in container.

methods.name: makeUnique
methods.desc:
Makes the feature and its geometry unique, thereby the geometry 
		 is not shared with other features.
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use the makeUnique() method in vcComponent.

properties.name: AmbientOcclusion
properties.desc:
Defines if geometry supporting ambient occlusion is rendered 
		 in the 3D world. 
		0
		VC_AMBIENT_OCCLUSION_NONE
		1
		VC_AMBIENT_OCCLUSION_VERTEX

properties.name: CreaseAngle
properties.desc:
Defines an angle tolerance for smoothing surfaces based on 
		 camera angle and lighting calculations. 
		For example, if the angle between edges 
		 of a surface is less than CreaseAngle, the affected triangle sets 
		 will appear as one smooth face.

properties.name: Geometry
properties.desc: Gets the container of feature's geometry.

properties.name: IsUnique
properties.desc:
Indicates if the feature and its geometry is unique or shared 
		 with other features.
		(Deprecated) 
		 Use the IsUnique property in vcComponent.

properties.name: Pickable
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the ability to select geometry of feature in the 
		 3D world. 
		Note: This affects 
		 all commands and tools that use snap types.

properties.name: ShowContent
properties.desc: Turns on/off the visibility of feature.

properties.name: ShowBackfaces
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the rendering of geometry in the feature that 
		 is not facing the camera of the 3D world.

properties.name: TesselationQuality
properties.desc:
Defines the quality of feature's geometry by affecting both 
		 angle and chord height tolerances used for tessellating the feature. 
		 
		Note: This property 
		 does not set any fractional tolerance values as it relates to 
		 the degree of accuracy.

properties.name: Uri
properties.desc:
Defines the URI of source file for geometry used in feature. 
		 
		Writing this property will override any 
		 existing geometry in the feature and cannot be undone.

methods.name: updateBoundIncrementally
methods.desc: Increments the bound box of the set's component.

properties.name: Billboard
properties.desc:
Defines if geometry of set is always facing the 3D world camera. 
		 
		Generally, this property is used for billboard 
		 text and is only supported for the following types:
		vcCompactLineSet
		vcPointSet
		vcText2DSet
		vcTriangleSet

properties.name: BoundCenter
properties.desc:
Gets a vector from the origin to the center of the container's 
		 bound box.

properties.name: BoundDiagonal
properties.desc:
Gets a half diagonal vector from the center to an upper corner 
		 of the container's bound box using positive axis directions.

properties.name: Container
properties.desc: Gets the geometry container of set.

properties.name: Feature
properties.desc: Gets the feature that the set belongs to in node feature tree.

properties.name: FixedSize
properties.desc:
Defines if the size of set visually remains the same in the 
		 3D world regardless of camera position. 
		This property is only supported for the 
		 following types:
		vcCompactLineSet
		vcPointSet
		vcText2DSet
		vcTriangleSet

properties.name: HasMaterialInheritance
properties.desc:
Determines if the geometry set has material inheritance (geo 
		 set will use the inherited material or its own).

properties.name: Layer
properties.desc: Defines the layer that the set belongs to in layout.

properties.name: LightAmbientTexture
properties.desc:
Defines if the material texture of set is used to affect ambient 
		 light intensity and shininess of surfaces. 
		(Deprecated)

properties.name: LightAmbientVertex
properties.desc:
Defines if vertex color/intensity is blended with light rays 
		 to render ambient lighting effect. 
		(Deprecated)

properties.name: Material
properties.desc:
Defines the material of set. 
		If None, the set uses default render settings.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of set.

properties.name: Type
properties.desc:
Gets the set type. 
		See Geometry 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: UseBackface
properties.desc:
Defines if geometry of set is rendered when not facing the 
		 3D world camera.

properties.name: VertexColor
properties.desc:
Defines if the set uses vertex coloring. 
		See Geometry 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: addElseIfScope
methods.desc:
Adds vcElseIfScope to the 
		 statement and returns that scope. 
		The default value of index 
		 is -1, so a new vcElseIfScope 
		 is inserted immediately before ElseScope.

methods.name: deleteElseIfScope
methods.desc:
Deletes given scope 
		 from the statement.

properties.name: Condition
properties.desc:
Defines an expression that when evaluated returns a True or 
		 False value. 
		A True value means the statement will execute 
		 its ThenScope of statements.
		A False value means the statement will execute 
		 its ElseScope of statements.

properties.name: ThenScope
properties.desc:
Gets the scope of statements executed by the statement if Condition 
		 is true.

properties.name: ElseIfScopes
properties.desc:
Gets a list of ElseIfScopes 
		 in the statement.

properties.name: ElseScope
properties.desc:
Gets the scope of statements executed by the statement if Condition 
		 is false.

methods.name: signal
methods.desc:
Signals the current value of signal to all connected behaviors, 
		 thereby triggering the OnSignal event. 
		An optional value 
		 argument can be given to set the Value property of the signal.

properties.name: Value
properties.desc:
Defines the value of signal. 
		Setting this value does not trigger the 
		 OnSignal event unless you use the signal() method.

methods.name: getPortName
methods.desc:
Returns the name of a port at a given index 
		 in map.

methods.name: input
methods.desc:
Returns the value of a port at a given index 
		 in map.

methods.name: output
methods.desc:
Sets the value of a port at a given index 
		 to a given value in map.

methods.name: setPortName
methods.desc:
Sets the name of a port at a given index 
		 to a given name in map.

properties.name: Listeners
properties.desc: Defines a list of behaviors using the signal map.

properties.name: PortCount
properties.desc: Defines the amount of ports in signal map.

properties.name: IsSystem
properties.desc: Always returns True

methods.name: inverse
methods.desc:
Calculates the joint values of robot for a given target 
		 and list of joint values. 
		An optional fixed 
		 argument can be given to identify fixed joints in the robot.
		The returned value will identify joint values 
		 of robot and status of solution to target.
		See Solution 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: ForwardKin
properties.desc:
Defines the function for forward kinematics calculation. 
		If None, uses built-in method.

properties.name: FractionalStep
properties.desc:
Defines the fractional step of calculation. 
		The default value is 0.5.

properties.name: IgnoreOrientation
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the calculation of orientation.
		The default value is False in which orientation 
		 is calculated for solution. 
		Generally, a True value would be used when 
		 orientation is not important, for example with Cartesian robots.

properties.name: JacobianJointCount
properties.desc: Defines the number of joints in calculation.

properties.name: NumIterationsInner
properties.desc: Defines the number of iterations for calculating inner product.

properties.name: NumIterationsOuter
properties.desc: Defines the number of iterations for calculating outer product.

properties.name: OrientationMaxStep
properties.desc: Defines the max step for orientation in calculation.

properties.name: OrientationTolerance
properties.desc: Defines the tolerance for orientation in calculation.

properties.name: PositionalMaxStep
properties.desc: Defines the max step for position in calculation.

properties.name: PositionalTolerance
properties.desc: Defines the tolerance for position in calculation.

properties.name: RotationalJointStepSize
properties.desc: Defines the step for rotational joint values in calculation.

properties.name: Controller
properties.desc:
Gets the controller of joint. 
		If joint is not driven by controller, value 
		 is None.

properties.name: CurrentValue
properties.desc: Defines the joint's value.

properties.name: Dof
properties.desc: Gets the Dof object of joint.

properties.name: ExternalController
properties.desc:
Gets the external controller of joint. 
		If joint is not driven by an external controller, 
		 value is None.

properties.name: InitialValue
properties.desc:
Defines the initial value of joint. That is, the initial state 
		 of the joint.

properties.name: LagTime
properties.desc: Defines the lag time (in seconds) of joint.

properties.name: MaxAcceleration
properties.desc:
Defines the maximum acceleration (units/degrees per second 
		 squared) of joint.

properties.name: MaxDeceleration
properties.desc:
Defines the maximum deceleration (units/degrees per second 
		 squared) of joint.

properties.name: MaxSpeed
properties.desc:
Defines the maximum speed (units/degrees per second squared) 
		 of joint.

properties.name: MaxValue
properties.desc:
Defines an expression that when evaluated returns the maximum 
		 value of joint.

properties.name: MinValue
properties.desc:
Defines an expression that when evaluated returns the minimum 
		 value of joint.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the joint's name.

properties.name: SettleTime
properties.desc: Defines the settle time (in seconds) of joint.

properties.name: Type
properties.desc:
Defines the joint type. 
See Joint Constants for more information.

methods.name: createJacobian
methods.desc:
Creates a new Jacobian matrix object for calculating inverse 
		 and forward kinematics solutions.

methods.name: createProperty
methods.desc:
Adds a new property of a given type 
		 and name to the kinematics object. 
		 
		An optional constraints 
		 argument can be given to define constraints for the new property, 
		 which must be defined at the time of creation.
		See Property 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: getJointMoveDist
methods.desc:
Returns the distance a joint at a given index 
		 must move in order to reach a given value.

methods.name: getJointMoveTo
methods.desc:
Indicates whether a joint at a given index 
		 can move to a given value. 
		Returns True and the given value if joint 
		 can reach target. Otherwise, returns False and the amount exceeding 
		 the joint's limits.

methods.name: moveJointTo
methods.desc:
Drives a joint at a given index 
		 to a given value. 
		Returns True if joint reached target; otherwise 
		 returns False.

properties.name: CustomData
properties.desc:
Defines an instance of a user-defined class, thereby allowing 
		 you to implement custom properties and methods for the kinematics 
		 object.

properties.name: JointCount
properties.desc: Gets the joint count of the kinematics object.

properties.name: JointMaxLimits
properties.desc: Gets the maximum value for each joint of the kinematics object.

properties.name: JointMinLimits
properties.desc: Gets the minimum value for each joint of the kinematics object.

properties.name: JointsRotational
properties.desc:
Gets the joint type for each joint of the kinematics object. 
		 
		A True value indicates a rotational joint.

properties.name: JointValues
properties.desc: Defines the joint values of the kinematics object.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc: Gets the dynamic properties of the kinematics object.

properties.name: SecondaryJointValues
properties.desc: Defines the external joint values of the kinematics object.

properties.name: Solutions
properties.desc:
Defines a list of possible solutions for the kinematics object 
		 and its Target. 
		Generally, the format of a solution is a 
		 configuration warning followed by joint values for the motion 
		 target.
		See Solution 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: Target
properties.desc: Defines the motion target of the kinematics object.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of layer.

properties.name: Visibility
properties.desc: Turns on/off the visibility of layer and all of its objects.

methods.name: update
methods.desc: Updates the item in its layout.

properties.name: IsPersistent
properties.desc: Defines if the item is saved with layout.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of item.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc: Gets a list of all properties for item.

properties.name: Type
properties.desc:
Defines the item type. 
		See Layout 
		 Item Constants for more information.

properties.name: PackFolder
properties.desc: Gets the mechanism for attaching files to component.

properties.name: createProperty
properties.desc:
Adds a new property of a given type 
		 and name to the layout item. 
		An optional constraints 
		 argument can be given to define constraints for the new property, 
		 which must be defined at the time of creation.
		See Property 
		 Constants for more information.

properties.name: deleteProperty
properties.desc: Deletes a given property from the item.

properties.name: getProperty
properties.desc: Returns a property of the item that matches the given name; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: DataCount
methods.desc: Gets the number of records in schema.

methods.name: FrameColorSchemaIndex
methods.desc:
Defines the index of schema property used for coloring frame. 
		 
		The schema property should be a vector data 
		 type.

methods.name: FrameDataSchemaIndex
methods.desc:
Defines the index of schema property used for positional data 
		 of record. 
		Generally, the schema property is a matrix 
		 data type. The positional data is used for visualizing record 
		 as a Frame feature in 3D world.

methods.name: FrameNameColorSchemaIndex
methods.desc:
Defines the index of schema property used for coloring the 
		 label of frame. 
		The schema property should be a vector data 
		 type.

methods.name: FrameNameSchemaIndex
methods.desc:
Defines the index of schema property used for labeling the 
		 Frame feature of record in 3D world. 
		The schema property should be a string data 
		 type.
		The default is -1. This means the Frame 
		 feature of record will not be labeled with its custom name rather 
		 the number of record in schema.

methods.name: FrameNameVisibleSchemaIndex
methods.desc:
Defines the index of schema property used for controlling 
		 the visibility of label of record in 3D world. 
		The schema property should be a Boolean 
		 data type.
		The default is -1. This means labels are 
		 visible.

methods.name: FrameVisibleSchemaIndex
methods.desc:
Defines the index of schema property used for controlling the 
		 visibility of Frame feature of record in 3D world. 
		The schema property should be a Boolean 
		 data type.
		This also affects the visibility of label 
		 of record in 3D world.

methods.name: LineDisplaySchemaIndex
methods.desc:
Define the index of schema property used for the position of 
		 record in 3D world. 
		  
		This allows you to connect positions with a line 
		 generated in 3D world.

methods.name: Node
methods.desc:
Defines a node the Frame features of records are attached to 
		 in 3D world. 
		In some cases, this might be the simulation 
		 root node/World node. In other cases, this might be the root node 
		 of a workpiece.

methods.name: PositionMatrix
methods.desc:
Defines an offset for position of record in 3D world. 
		The offset is based in coordinate system 
		 of Node property.
		Generally, an offset is applied to compensate 
		 for weld torch flares or to adjust position based on Z-axis direction 
		 of robot TCP.

methods.name: SchemaProperties
methods.desc:
Gets a list of all schema properties in the layout item. 
		Note: This does 
		 not include data values for each record in the schema.

methods.name: clearSchema
methods.desc:
Empties the schema, thereby removing all schema properties 
		 and setting the data count to zero.

methods.name: cloneSchemaObject
methods.desc:
Clones a set of records in a given range. 
		The from_dataindex 
		 argument defines the first record in range. The count 
		 argument defines how many records to clone. The to_dataindex 
		 argument defines where to insert the copies.
		Warning: Currently, 
		 you cannot append cloned records to the end of the table. You 
		 must insert the copies before an existing record.

methods.name: createProperty
methods.desc:
Adds a new property of a given type 
		 and name to the layout item. 
		An optional constraints 
		 argument can be given to define constraints for the new property, 
		 which must be defined at the time of creation.
		See Property 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: createSchemaProperty
methods.desc:
Adds a new schema property of a given type 
		 and name to the layout item. 
		See Property 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: deleteProperty
methods.desc:
Deletes a given property of the 
		 layout item.

methods.name: deleteSchemaObject
methods.desc:
Deletes a set of records in a given range. 
		The from_dataindex 
		 argument defines the first record in range. The count 
		 argument defines how many records to delete.

methods.name: deleteSchemaProperty
methods.desc:
Deletes a given property that is 
		 a schema property of the layout item.

methods.name: getDataValue
methods.desc:
Returns the value of a data field at a given dataindex 
		 and itemindex.

methods.name: getDataValues
methods.desc: Returns the values of a record at a given dataindex.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc:
Returns a property of the layout item that matches the given 
		 name; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: getSchemaProperty
methods.desc:
Returns a schema property of the layout item that matches the 
		 given name; otherwise returns None.

methods.name: setDataValue
methods.desc:
Sets the value of a data field at a given dataindex 
		 and itemindex. 
		The value argument 
		 must be a supported data type and match the type of the schema 
		 property; otherwise the data field will not reference the new 
		 value. 
		Note: The value argument can be a vcProperty 
		 object, thereby the value of that property is passed to the data 
		 field.

methods.name: setDataValues
methods.desc:
Sets all values for schema properties of a record at a given 
		 dataindex. 
		The values argument 
		 must be a tuple with the same amount of elements as there are 
		 schema properties. Each element's value must be a supported data 
		 type and match the type of the corresponding schema property; 
		 otherwise the data field will not reference the new value.
		Note: An element 
		 of a tuple given as the values argument 
		 can be a vcProperty object, thereby 
		 the value of that property is passed to the data field.

methods.name: updateData
methods.desc:
Allocates the size of the schema to support a potential amount 
		 of elements/entries for schema properties based on the given count. 
		Note: The allocation 
		 is optional as size is updated automatically based on number of 
		 entries.

properties.name: Data Record 0
properties.desc: Data field (0,2)

properties.name: Data Record 1
properties.desc: Data field (1,2)
