properties.desc: Turns on or off the midpoint of edges as potential targets.

properties.name: SnapOnFaceCenter
properties.desc: Turns on or off the center of faces as potential targets.

properties.name: SnapOnFrame
properties.desc: Turns on or off frames as potential targets.

properties.name: SnapOnNodeCenter
properties.desc: Turns on or off the center of nodes as potential targets.

properties.name: SnapOnNodeOrigin
properties.desc: Turns on or off the origin of nodes as potential targets.

properties.name: SnapOnPoint
properties.desc:
Turns on or off points on lines and polygons, for example corner 
		 points, as potential targets.

properties.name: SnapOnPolygon
properties.desc: Turns on or off polygons as potential targets.

properties.name: SnapOnSurface
properties.desc: Turns on or off faces as potential targets.

properties.name: TargetAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if pointing at an available target in the 3D world.

properties.name: TargetCircleCenterAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if center of a circle is available as a target.

properties.name: TargetCurve
properties.desc:
Provides a list of positions for a target curve in World coordinate 
		 system.

properties.name: TargetCurveAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if a curve is available as a target.

properties.name: TargetCurveIndex
properties.desc:
Indicates the index position of a target curve in a geometry 
		 set.

properties.name: TargetFaceCenterAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if the center of a face is available as a target.

properties.name: TargetGeoset
properties.desc: Indicates the geometry set of a target.

properties.name: TargetLocked
properties.desc: Indicates if a target has been selected in the 3D world.

properties.name: TargetMatrix
properties.desc:
Indicates the position and orientation matrix for target in 
		 World coordinates.

properties.name: TargetMatrixAvailable
properties.desc:
Indicates if the position and orientation matrix for a target 
		 is available. (only valid for frame type targets)

properties.name: TargetNode
properties.desc: Indicates the node containing a target.

properties.name: TargetNormal
properties.desc: Indicates the normal vector of a target in World coordinates.

properties.name: TargetNormalAvailable
properties.desc:
Indicates if the normal vector of a target is available. (only 
		 valid for polygon and frame type targets).

properties.name: TargetPosition
properties.desc: Indicates the position of a target in World coordinates.

properties.name: TargetPrimitive
properties.desc: Indicates the geometry primitive object of a target.

properties.name: TargetSurfaceAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if the surface of a target is available.

properties.name: TargetSurfaceIndex
properties.desc:
Indicates the index position of a target surface in a component, 
		 for example the faces of a cube.

methods.name: createProperty
methods.desc:
Creates a new property of a given type 
		 and name in the statement, and then 
		 returns the new property. 
		An optional constraints 
		 argument can be used to define constraints for new property, which 
		 must be defined at the time of creation.
		See Property 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: deleteProperty
methods.desc:
Deletes a given property in the 
		 statement.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc:
Returns a property matching a given name 
		 in the statement; otherwise returns None.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of the statement.

properties.name: ParentScope
properties.desc: Gets the scope of the statement.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc: Gets a list of properties of the statement.

properties.name: ParentRoutine
properties.desc: Gets the routine of the statement.

properties.name: Type
properties.desc:
Gets the statement's type. 
		See Statement 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: PartsAverageCount
methods.desc:
Gets the average amount of components that have been contained 
		 in a component.

methods.name: PartsAverageTime
methods.desc: Gets the average amount of time components spent in a component.

methods.name: PartsCurrent
methods.desc: Gets the current amount of components contained in a component.

methods.name: PartsEntered
methods.desc:
Gets/Sets the number of components that have been transferred 
		 into a component. 
		Generally, this property is set to reset 
		 a count or collect from the start of a new process.

methods.name: PartsExited
methods.desc:
Gets/Sets the number of components that have been transferred 
		 out of a component. 
		Generally, this property is set to reset 
		 a count or collect from the start of a new process.

methods.name: PartsMaxCount
methods.desc:
Gets the maximum number of components that have been contained 
		 in a component at any given time.

methods.name: PartsMaxTime
methods.desc:
Gets the maximum amount of time a component has spent in a 
		 component.

methods.name: PartsMinCount
methods.desc:
Gets the minimum number of components that have been contained 
		 in a component at any given time.

methods.name: PartsMinTime
methods.desc:
Gets the minimum amount of time a component has spent in a 
		 component.

methods.name: PartsTotalTime
methods.desc:
Gets sum total of the amount of time each component had spent 
		 in a component, for example the duration of each component on 
		 a conveyor added together.

methods.name: PartsUtilization
methods.desc:
Gets the percentage of a component's capacity being utilized: 
		 number of parts divided by component's capacity.

methods.name: PartsIntervalAverageCount
methods.desc:
Same as other 
		 flow type properties, yet each value reflects the last recorded 
		 interval during a simulation, which by default is every 60.0 seconds. 
		 
		  
		See vcStatisticsManager 
		 for more information on how to change interval.

methods.name: AverageActivePeriodTime
methods.desc:
Gets the average amount of time a component was in one of its 
		 defined states.

methods.name: BlockedPercentage
methods.desc:
Gets the amount of time a component spent in a blocked state, 
		 for example capacity issue, as a percentage of total time.

methods.name: BreakPercentage
methods.desc:
Gets the amount of time a component spent in a broken state 
		 as a percentage of total time.

methods.name: BusyPercentage
methods.desc:
Gets the amount of time a component spent in a busy state or 
		 was being used as a percentage of total time.

methods.name: FailedPercentage
methods.desc:
Gets the amount of time a component spent in a failed state 
		 as a percentage of total time.

methods.name: IdlePercentage
methods.desc:
Gets the amount of time a component spent in an idle state 
		 as a percentage of total time.

methods.name: RepairPercentage
methods.desc:
Gets the amount of time a component spent in a repair state 
		 as a percentage of total time. 
		Scripting can be used to set repair time 
		 and include time waiting for a repair.

methods.name: SetupPercentage
methods.desc:
Gets the amount of time a component spent in a setup state, 
		 for example warm up time, as a percentage of total time.

methods.name: State
methods.desc:
Defines the current state of component. 
		Use the States property to get an indication 
		 of available states in component.

methods.name: State<name>Percentage
methods.desc:
Gets the amount of time a component spent in a user-defined 
		 state as a percentage of total time. 
		For example, StateExamplePercentage 
		 would refer to defined state called Example.

methods.name: TotalStateTime
methods.desc:
Gets the total amount of time a component was in one of its 
		 defined states based on total time.

methods.name: Utilization
methods.desc:
Gets the amount of time a component was busy during a simulation 
		 as a percentage (busy state/100 * 100%).

methods.name: IntervalBlockedPercentage
methods.desc:
Same as other 
		 state based properties, yet each value reflects the last recorded 
		 interval during a simulation, which by default is every 60.0 seconds. 
		 
		See vcStatisticsManager 
		 for more information on how to change interval.

methods.name: flowEnter
methods.desc:
Manually records a given component 
		 transferring into component.

methods.name: flowLeave
methods.desc:
Manually records a given component 
		 transferring out of component.

methods.name: getIntervalPercentage
methods.desc:
Returns the accumulated time of a given state 
		 as a percentage of the last recorded interval during a simulation.

methods.name: getPercentage
methods.desc:
Returns the accumulated time of a given state 
		 as a percentage of total time at the time of call.

methods.name: getSystemIntervalPercentage
methods.desc:
Returns the accumulated time of a given system_state 
		 as a percentage of the last recorded interval during a simulation.

methods.name: getSystemPercentage
methods.desc:
Returns the accumulated time of a given system_state 
		 as a percentage of total time at the time of call.

methods.name: getSystemTime
methods.desc:
Returns the accumulated time of a given system_state 
		 at the time of call.

methods.name: getTime
methods.desc:
Returns the accumulated time of a given state 
		 at the time of call.

methods.name: warmupCompleted
methods.desc:
Marks the completion/end of a component's warm up period, thereby 
		 setting all statistics to zero at the time of call.
		For example, a component can be configured 
		 to run a delay or a certain number of time consuming tasks at 
		 the start of a simulation. When this method is called, warm up 
		 time is calculated from simulation start to time of call.

properties.name: ComponentMaxCount
properties.desc:
Gets the maximum number of components that have been contained 
		 in a component at any given time.

properties.name: ComponentMaxTime
properties.desc:
Gets the maximum amount of time a component spent contained 
		 in a component.

properties.name: ComponentMinCount
properties.desc:
Gets the minimum number of components that been contained in 
		 a component at any given time.

properties.name: ComponentMinTime
properties.desc:
Gets the minimum amount of time a component spent contained 
		 in a component.

properties.name: ComponentsArrived
properties.desc:
Gets the total number of components that have been transferred 
		 into a component.

properties.name: ComponentsAverageTime
properties.desc:
Gets the average amount of time components have spent in a 
		 component.

properties.name: ComponentsCurrent
properties.desc:
Gets the total number of components currently contained in 
		 a component.

properties.name: ComponentsDeparted
properties.desc:
Gets the total amount of components that have been transferred 
		 out of a component.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of Statistics behavior.

properties.name: States
properties.desc:
Defines a list of defined states mapped to system states. 
		A state must be mapped to a system state. 
		 See Statistics 
		 for more information.

properties.name: SystemStates
properties.desc:
Gets a list of available system states, which provides system 
		 state description and type. 
		See Statistics 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: addSeries
methods.desc: Adds a new data series to chart.

methods.name: clearData
methods.desc: Removes all data reported by chart, thereby emptying DataRows.

methods.name: clearSeries
methods.desc: Resets all data series in chart, thereby emptying AllSources.

methods.name: deleteSeries
methods.desc:
Deletes a given data_series from 
		 chart.

methods.name: update
methods.desc: Refreshes the chart.

properties.name: AllSources
properties.desc:
Gets all sources of reported items, including their components. 
		 
		A reported item is a vcProperty 
		 object associated with a component. For example, a reported item 
		 could be a component property or a property of a component behavior.
		A vcVector object 
		 is used to define the display color of reported item in chart.

properties.name: ChartTileType
properties.desc:
Defines the location type of chart, thereby indicating whether 
		 the tile is an empty or filled with a chart. 
		Generally, you would use ChartTileType to 
		 parse through several charts in a dashboard to collect data from 
		 charts that report items. For example, you could ignore or skip 
		 empty tiles.

properties.name: ChartType
properties.desc:
Defines the chart type. 
		For more information, see Statistics 
		 Constants.

properties.name: DataRows
properties.desc: Gets the data collected during a simulation from reported items.

properties.name: DataType
properties.desc:
Defines the data type of chart. 
		For more information, see Statistics 
		 Constants.

properties.name: FieldCountPerProperty
properties.desc: Defines the field count of items reported by chart.

properties.name: LegendVisibility
properties.desc: Turns on/off the display of chart legend.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the title of chart.

properties.name: Position
properties.desc: Defines the position chart in tab grid.

properties.name: RecordAccumulatedValues
properties.desc: Turns on/off the collection of data reported by chart.

properties.name: SamplingInterval
properties.desc:
Defines how often (in seconds) the chart updates to show recorded 
		 data during a simulation. 
		If -1, the chart uses the sampling interval 
		 of its dashboard.

properties.name: Series
properties.desc: Gets a list of data series used by chart to report items.

properties.name: TileType
properties.desc:
Same as ChartTileType. 
		For more information, see Statistics 
		 Constants.

properties.name: TitleVisibility
properties.desc: Turns on/off the display of chart title.

methods.name: createTab
methods.desc:
Adds a new tab of a given name to the dashboard.
The activate argument can be used to make the new tab the selected tab in dashboard.

methods.name: deleteTab
methods.desc: Removes a given tab from the dashboard.

properties.name: SelectedTab
properties.desc: Defines the active tab in dashboard.

properties.name: StatisticsInterval
properties.desc:
Defines the global sampling interval for reporting data.
This will affect data series referencing vcStatistics properties as well as any chart with a sampling interval of -1.

properties.name: Tabs
properties.desc: Gets a list of all tabs in dashboard.

properties.name: SamplingInterval
properties.desc:
Defines the sampling interval used by simulation for recording 
		 interval based statistics.
		The default rate is 60.0 seconds, so an 
		 interval is recorded every 60 seconds in simulation.

properties.name: Colors
properties.desc:
Defines the colors of series, which is displayed in chart.
For example, data collected from different components should be color-coded to differentiate their data in chart.

properties.name: Components
properties.desc:
Defines the components the series collects data from during a simulation.
In order to collect data, a listed component must have Property.

properties.name: Expression
properties.desc: Defines the expression of series.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of series object.

properties.name: ParentChart
properties.desc: Gets the chart of series.

properties.name: Property
properties.desc: Defines the reported item (source) of series.

properties.name: SeriesName
properties.desc: Defines the name of series, which is displayed in chart legend.

properties.name: Sources
properties.desc:
Gets a list of sources for series data.
This information includes the reported item (vcProperty) and its component.

properties.name: Thickness
properties.desc: Defines the display thickness of series, for example the line thickness of data collected from different components.

methods.name: clearLayout
methods.desc: Deletes all charts from tab grid.

methods.name: createChart
methods.desc:
Adds a new chart of a given type to tab grid. 
		The location 
		 argument specifies where in grid to insert the new chart. In this 
		 context, the vcStatisticsChart 
		 object is a grid location. It can be a chart with existing data 
		 or an empty chart used as a placeholder. In either case, a call 
		 will remove the existing chart and exchange it with a new one 
		 in the grid.
		The activate 
		 argument can be used to make the new chart the active chart in 
		 tab.
		For more information on the chart_type 
		 argument, see Statistics 
		 Constants.

methods.name: createLayout
methods.desc: Creates a new layout for tab grid.

methods.name: deleteChart
methods.desc:
Removes a chart from tab grid, thereby replacing the old chart 
		 with a new empty chart used as a placeholder in grid.

methods.name: selectChart
methods.desc:
Selects a chart in tab, thereby making it the active chart 
		 in tab.

properties.name: Charts
properties.desc: Defines the charts of tab.

properties.name: Layouts
properties.desc: Defines the available layouts for tab grid.

properties.name: MaxColumns
properties.desc: Defines the maximum number of columns in tab grid.

properties.name: MaxRows
properties.desc: Defines the maximum number of rows in tab grid.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of tab.

properties.name: SelectedChart
properties.desc: Defines the active chart of tab.

properties.name: SelectedLayout
properties.desc: Defines the current layout of tab grid.

properties.name: SelectedLayoutItem
properties.desc:
Defines the attributes of SelectedLayout. 
		Note: A layout 
		 has a name and a list for each of its placeholders/tiles. A placeholder 
		 defines the grid column and row size of a chart.

methods.name: signal
methods.desc:
Signals the current value of signal to all connected behaviors, 
		 thereby triggering the OnSignal event. 
		An optional value 
		 argument can be given to set the Value property of the signal.

properties.name: Value
properties.desc:
Defines the value of signal. 
		Setting this value does not trigger the 
		 OnSignal event unless you use the signal() method.

methods.name: input
methods.desc: Returns the value of a port at a given index.

methods.name: output
methods.desc:
Sets the value of a port at a given index 
		 to a given value.

properties.name: Listeners
properties.desc: Defines a list of behaviors using the signal map.

properties.name: PortCount
properties.desc: Defines the amount of ports in the signal map.

methods.name: begin
methods.desc:
Starts swept volume process, thereby initiating decomposition. 
		 
		An optional vector 
		 argument can be given to define a frame of reference or center 
		 point in input node. If not, process uses center point of input 
		 node bound box.

methods.name: clear
methods.desc: Removes all swept geometry of layout item from 3D world.

methods.name: end
methods.desc:
Stops swept volume process. 
		After swept volume process has ended, you 
		 can perform capping of swept geometry.

methods.name: next
methods.desc:
Executes an iterative process that renders swept geometry based 
		 on positions of input nodes. That is, you should call this method 
		 each time you want to render swept volume in 3D world during swept 
		 process. 
		An optional vector 
		 argument can be given to define a frame of reference or center 
		 point in input node as it moves during a simulation. If not, process 
		 uses center point of input node bound box. Generally, this is 
		 used to offset swept geometry.

methods.name: store
methods.desc:
Stores swept geometry in TargetNode, thereby allowing you to 
		 save swept geometry in component and/or layout. 
		Returns the Geometry feature where swept 
		 volume is stored in TargetNode. The naming convention for feature 
		 is VC_SweptVolumeResult, and the feature is an immediate child 
		 of TargetNode root feature.
		If no swept geometry is generated during 
		 simulation, returns None.
		Generally, you should call store() method 
		 after calling end() method and before clear() method.

properties.name: Decomposition
properties.desc:
Defines the number of convex hulls created for included nodes, 
		 for example one conveyor hull encompassing all nodes or several 
		 convex hulls based on geometry of each node. 
		0
		One convex hull.
		1
		One or more convex hulls using convex decomposition.
		2
		One convex hull for each triangle mesh in input nodes.
		See Decomposition 
		 Modes for more information.

properties.name: DecompositionDecimationTarget
properties.desc:
If Decomposition set to 1, sets the number of triangle sets 
		 remaining after decimation process of input nodes with fewer triangle 
		 sets than decimation target, thereby allowing you to expedite/speed 
		 up the process. 
		Set to zero to have no effect.

properties.name: DecompositionQuality
properties.desc:
If Decomposition set to 1, sets the quality of decomposition 
		 in range 0 to 100, thereby affecting the approximation of convex 
		 hulls to the shape of input node geometry. 
		A higher value produces better approximation 
		 and convex-shaped triangle sets at the cost of increasing a component's 
		 data count and simulation performance.

properties.name: InputNodeList
properties.desc:
Defines which nodes will be swept during a simulation. 
		The value type is similar to Nodes property 
		 of a vcNodeList object in which a 
		 given node and its scope is either included or excluded from swept 
		 volume.

properties.name: Method
properties.desc:
Sets the method used for generating convex hulls as swept geometry, 
		 for example hollow or filled convex hulls. 
		0
		Uses lofting. Good for movements requiring small changes, for example 
		 small rotational and directional changes in linear motions and 
		 bending of curves.
		1
		Uses hull from hulls generation. Creates internal faces and more 
		 points, thereby a higher data count but supports all types of 
		 movement.
		2
		Uses hull from silhouettes generation. Balance of methods 0 and 
		 1 to support small and complex movements.
		Note: Each method 
		 type has about the same performance level.
		See Swept 
		 Generation for more information.

properties.name: TargetNode
properties.desc:
Sets the node used for containing swept geometry, which should 
		 be static and not move during simulation.

methods.name: addCase
methods.desc:
Creates a new case and appends it to the end.
		or
		Creates a new case and inserts it to the given index. If index 
		 is less than zero or greater than the current case count, the 
		 case will be appended to the end.
		or
		Inserts an existing case to the given index. If index is less 
		 than zero or greater than the current case count, the case will 
		 be appended to the end.

methods.name: moveCase
methods.desc:
Moves an existing case to the new position. If the given index 
		 is less than zero or greater than the current case count, the 
		 case will be moved to the end.

methods.name: deleteCase
methods.desc: Removes an existing case and deletes it.

methods.name: releaseCase
methods.desc: Removes an existing case.

methods.name: getCase
methods.desc: Gets an existing case.

properties.name: Condition
properties.desc:
Expression that defines the value against which the case 
		 conditions are evaluated. 
		See also Process 
		 Statement Expressions and Robot 
		 Statements.

properties.name: Cases
properties.desc:
All case scopes in this statement. Each scope has an RW property 
		 CaseCondition of type String which will be evaluated against statement's 
		 Condition.

methods.name: setActiveStatement
methods.desc: Sets the statement at the given index in the given scope to be ActiveStatement.

properties.name: ActiveRobot
properties.desc: Defines the active robot in context.

properties.name: ActiveRoutine
properties.desc: Gets the active routine in the ActiveRobot program.

properties.name: ActiveScope
properties.desc:
Gets the active routine or scope of statement in ActiveRobot 
		 program.

properties.name: ActiveStatement
properties.desc: Gets the active statement in ActiveRobot program.

properties.name: ActiveStatementIndex
properties.desc: Gets the index of active statement in ActiveRobot program.

methods.name: getTextHeight
methods.desc: Returns the calculated height of text in pixels.

methods.name: getTextWidth
methods.desc: Returns the calculated width of text in pixels.

methods.name: update
methods.desc: Updates the geometry of text in 3D world.

properties.name: DepthBuffered
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the obstruction of text by other objects that 
		 are in front of it on screen.
		If False, text is always set to front of 
		 foreground.

properties.name: OffsetX
properties.desc:
Defines an offset (in pixels) for horizontal axis when text 
		 is projected on screen.

properties.name: OffsetY
properties.desc:
Defines an offset (in pixels) for vertical axis when text is 
		 projected on screen.

properties.name: Position
properties.desc:
Defines the position vector of text in 3D world.
		Text is rendered in which left end of its 
		 baseline coincides with Position on screen. If OffsetX or OffsetY 
		 are non-zero values, position is shifted by those values.

properties.name: Text
properties.desc: Defines a string of characters to render as one line of text.

methods.name: getTextHeight
methods.desc: Returns the calculated height of text in pixels.

methods.name: getTextWidth
methods.desc: Returns the calculated width of text in pixels.

methods.name: update
methods.desc: Updates the geometry of text in 3D world.

properties.name: Matrix
properties.desc: Defines the position matrix of text.

properties.name: OffsetX
properties.desc:
Defines an offset (in pixels) for horizontal axis when text 
		 is projected on screen.

properties.name: OffsetY
properties.desc:
Defines an offset (in pixels) for vertical axis when text is 
		 projected on screen.

properties.name: Text
properties.desc:
Defines a string of characters to render as a one line of 3D 
		 text.

methods.name: addTool
methods.desc:
Adds a new tool frame to container, and then returns the new 
		 tool frame.

methods.name: removeTool
methods.desc: Removes a given tool frame from container.

properties.name: Tools
properties.desc: Gets a list of all tool frames referenced by container.

properties.name: IPOMode
properties.desc:
Defines the interpolation mode of the frame and the external 
		 configuration of a referencing robot controller. 
		0
		Default setting, so no effect on robot's external configuration.
		1
		Robot position inherits orientation of base frame.
		2
		Robot position inherits orientation of tool frame.
		Interpolation 
		 constants can be used with this property.
		Note: A conflict 
		 can occur if a base-tool pair in a referencing robot have the 
		 same IPOMode property value or cannot be used with the robot's 
		 current configuration.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of the frame.

properties.name: Node
properties.desc: Defines the node the frame is attached to in the 3D world.

properties.name: PositionMatrix
properties.desc:
Defines the frame's position and orientation in the Node property's 
		 coordinate system. 
		The position matrix is a result of the node's 
		 offset, pivot and joint expressions but can be set manually.

properties.name: PositionExpression
properties.desc: The matrix offset expression for the frame's location.

methods.name: brepAvailable
methods.desc:
Returns True if set contains boundary representation; otherwise 
		 returns False.

methods.name: createCurveLoop
methods.desc:
Adds a new curve loop to a face at a given index in set, and 
		 then returns the index of new curve loop in set.

methods.name: createNurbsFace
methods.desc:
Adds a new non-uniform b-spline surface (NURBS) to set, and 
		 then returns the index of new surface in set.

methods.name: createPlanarFace
methods.desc:
Adds a new planar (unlimited) face using given position and 
		 surface normal vectors, and then returns the index of new face 
		 in set.

methods.name: createOffsetSurface
methods.desc:
Creates a copy of face at a given index in set, and then returns 
		 the index of new face in a given geometry set. 
		New face is offset from original face. If 
		 offset argument is positive value, 
		 new face is offset in surface normal direction; otherwise offset 
		 is the opposite direction of surface normal.

methods.name: createTrimPolyLine
methods.desc:
Creates a new polyline using a curve loop at a given index 
		 in set, which can then be used for trimming and extending operations, 
		 and polyline is surface domain (XY coordinates only). 
		The returned value is the index of trim 
		 polyline in set.

methods.name: createTrimSpline
methods.desc:
Create a new spline in set used for trimming and extending 
		 operations, and spline is surface domain (XY coordinates only).

methods.name: deleteNurbFace
methods.desc:
Deletes a NURBS face at a given index in set. 
		If NURBS surface contains more than one 
		 face, geometry is tessellated after deletion.

methods.name: getCurveCurveLoop
methods.desc:
Returns the index of curve loop that a curve belongs to in 
		 set.

methods.name: getCurveFace
methods.desc: Returns the index of face that a curve belongs to in set.

methods.name: getCurveIntersections
methods.desc:
Returns a list of curve intersection points based on given 
		 arguments.

methods.name: getCurveLength
methods.desc:
Returns the length of a curve at a given index in set. That 
		 is, the total distance along the curve.

methods.name: getCurveLoopCurve
methods.desc:
Returns the absolute index of an inner curve loop relative 
		 to its curve loop in set.

methods.name: getCurveLoopCurveCount
methods.desc:
Returns the total number of inner curve loops for a curve loop 
		 of face in set.

methods.name: getCurveNeighbor
methods.desc: Returns the index of a curve neighboring another curve in set.

methods.name: getCurvePointCount
methods.desc:
Returns the total number of points for a curve at a given index 
		 in set.

methods.name: getCurvePointIndex
methods.desc:
Returns the absolute index of point relative to its curve in 
		 set.

methods.name: getCurvePosition
methods.desc:
Returns the position matrix of a point on a curve at a given 
		 distance along curve. 
		Details about the position matrix:
		Position vector
		Actual position of point on curve.
		Normal vector
		Direction of curve at the given point (derivative of curve position).
		Orientation vector
		Aligned to face inwards of curve's face.
		Approach vector
		Surface normal of face at curve position.
		See table footnotes for more information.

methods.name: getCurvePositions
methods.desc:
Returns a list of position matrices for points along a curve 
		 using different criteria. 
		The minstep 
		 and maxstep arguments define the step 
		 values along distance of curve for generating new points.
		The maxerror 
		 argument defines a maximum distance error along length of curve 
		 for generating a new point.
		The maxangle 
		 argument defines a angle tolerance along curve for generating 
		 new points.
		See table footnotes for more information.

methods.name: getCurveType
methods.desc:
Returns a trim curve's type, which is either a polyline or 
		 spline. 
		See Topology 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: getFaceBound
methods.desc:
Returns bound box data for a face as an ordered pair (position 
		 matrix of bound box center, vector of bound box half-diagonal). 
		 
		See table footnotes for more information.

methods.name: getFaceCurveLoop
methods.desc:
Returns the absolute index of a curve loop relative to its 
		 face in set.

methods.name: getFaceCurveLoopCount
methods.desc: Returns the total number of curve loops in a face.

methods.name: getFaceMinPointDistance
methods.desc:
Returns UV coordinates, position vector and distance of a given 
		 point to a face.

methods.name: getFaceNormal
methods.desc: Returns surface normal of a face at parametric UV coordinates.

methods.name: getFacePlaneIntersections
methods.desc:
Returns a list containing lists of position matrices for points 
		 where a defined plane intersects a face. 
		Each time a plane goes through hole in face 
		 a new list is added, thereby allowing you to infer hole points 
		 on face-plane intersection.
		Details about the position matrix:
		Position vector
		Actual position of point intersection.
		Normal vector
		Direction along plane intersecting face.
		Orientation vector
		Projected from normal of plane to surface of face using face derivate 
		 for projected direction.
		Approach vector
		Surface normal of face.
		See table footnotes for more information.

methods.name: getFacePoint
methods.desc:
Returns the position vector of a point on a face at given UV 
		 coordinates.

methods.name: getFacePointAndDerivate
methods.desc:
Returns the position vector and UV direction first derivates 
		 of a face at given UV coordinates.

methods.name: getFaceStartTriangle
methods.desc: Returns the absolute index of first triangle of a face in set.

methods.name: getFaceTriangleCount
methods.desc: Returns the total number of triangles of a face.

methods.name: getFaceType
methods.desc:
Returns the type of a face, which is either a tessellated, 
		 planar or NURBS. 
		See Topology 
		 Constants for more information.

methods.name: getNurbsFaceControlPoints
methods.desc: Returns a list of control points for a NURBS face.

methods.name: getNurbsFaceControlWeights
methods.desc: Returns a list of control weights for a NURBS face.

methods.name: getNurbsFaceDegree
methods.desc: Returns UV degree values for a NURBS face.

methods.name: getNurbsFaceUKnots
methods.desc: Returns U direction knot weight values and knot multiplicities.

methods.name: getNurbsFaceVKnots
methods.desc: Returns V direction knot weight values and knot multiplicities.

methods.name: getPlanarFacePositionAndNormal
methods.desc: Returns a planar face position and normal vectors.

methods.name: getPolyLineCurvePoints
methods.desc: Returns a list of position vectors for all points in a polyline.

methods.name: getPoint
methods.desc:
Returns the position vector of a curve end (corner point) at 
		 a given index relative to either its curve or face.

methods.name: getSplineCurveDegree
methods.desc: Returns the degree of a spline.

methods.name: getSplineCurveControlPoints
methods.desc: Returns a list of control points for a face trimming spline.

methods.name: getSplineCurveControlWeights
methods.desc:
Returns a list of control weight values for a face trimming 
		 spline.

methods.name: getSplineCurveKnots
methods.desc:
Returns a list of knot weights and multiplicities for a face 
		 trimming spline as an ordered pair.

methods.name: getSurfaceIntersections
methods.desc:
Returns the amount of intersecting curves between two faces 
		 in the same vcGeometryContainer 
		 object.

methods.name: isCurveCircular
methods.desc:
Returns True if a curve at a given index in set is circular 
		 where start and end points are same; otherwise returns False.

methods.name: isFaceLinear
methods.desc:
Returns True if a face at a given index in set is linear in 
		 parametric UV directions; otherwise returns False.

methods.name: projectCurve
methods.desc:
Projects a given curve along the 
		 shape of a given face based on direction 
		 vector of curve.

methods.name: trimFace
methods.desc:
Trims a face at a given index in set using trimming polylines 
		 and/or splines. 
		Returns 1/True if trimming is successful; 
		 otherwise returns 0/False.

properties.name: CurveCount
properties.desc: Gets the total number of curves in set.

properties.name: CurveLoopCount
properties.desc: Gets the total number of curve loops in set.

properties.name: FaceCount
properties.desc: Gets the total number of faces in set.

properties.name: PointCount
properties.desc:
Gets the total number of points considered boundary-corners 
		 in mesh, for example curve ends. If set is not a mesh, gives zero.
		 
		Note: To get 
		 the total number of points in set, use PointCount in vcTriangleSet.

properties.name: ContinuousMode
properties.desc: Turns on/off the use of continuous curve selection in 3D world.

properties.name: SnapOnCurve
properties.desc: Turns on/off the ability to select a curve.

properties.name: SnapOnCurveLoop
properties.desc: Turns on/off the ability to select a curve loop.

properties.name: SnapOnSurface
properties.desc: Turns on/off the ability to select a point on a face.

properties.name: TargetAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if pointing at a valid target.

properties.name: TargetCurveAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if pointing at an available curve.

properties.name: TargetCurveIndex
properties.desc: Gets the index of an available curve.

properties.name: TargetCurveLoopAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if pointing at an available curve loop.

properties.name: TargetCurveLoopIndex
properties.desc: Gets the index of an available curve loop.

properties.name: TargetCurves
properties.desc: Gets a list of curve data for target.

properties.name: TargetGeoset
properties.desc: Gets geometry set of a target.

properties.name: TargetLocked
properties.desc: Indicates if target has been selected in 3D world.

properties.name: TargetNode
properties.desc: Gets the node containing target.

properties.name: TargetNormal
properties.desc: If available, gets surface normal of target.

properties.name: TargetNormalAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if surface normal is available for target.

properties.name: TargetPosition
properties.desc: Gets the position vector of target in World coordinate system.

properties.name: TargetSurfaceAvailable
properties.desc: Indicates if pointing at an available point on surface.

properties.name: TargetSurfaceIndex
properties.desc: Gets the index of an available surface.

properties.name: ParentMatrix
properties.desc:
Defines the origin of command's local coordinate system in 
		 3D world.
		Generally, this would be the position matrix 
		 of a selected object or an desired offset.

properties.name: UseAbsoluteCoordSystem
properties.desc:
Turns on/off the use of World coordinate system as opposed 
		 to command's local coordinate system.

properties.name: UseHandles
properties.desc: Turns on/off the use of a manipulator.

properties.name: WorldMatrix
properties.desc:
Defines position matrix of command's origin in 3D world, which 
		 can be used to set an initial position and orientation for command 
		 execution.

properties.name: WorldPosition
properties.desc:
Defines the position vector of command in World coordinate 
		 system.

properties.name: setTargetInfo
properties.access:
Enumeration availability, vcNode 
		 node, vcContainer 
		 container, vcMatrix 
		 location
properties.desc:
Sets target information for a transportation action.
		The availability 
		 argument is used to notify resource of target/pick up container 
		 status. See Transportation 
		 Constants for more information.
		The node or 
		 container argument should be used 
		 to specify a buffer area.
		The location 
		 argument is used to specify the location of a delivered component 
		 in either node or container.

properties.name: IsSystem
properties.desc: True if this controller is part of the application.

methods.name: createProperty
methods.desc:
Creates a new dynamic property to this 
		 transport link.

methods.name: getProperty
methods.desc: Returns a property from this transport link.

methods.name: deleteProperty
methods.desc: Deletes a property from this transport link.

properties.name: Source
properties.desc: The transport node to start moving from.

properties.name: Destination
properties.desc: The destination transport node.

properties.name: Implementer
properties.desc:
The controller that will take care of moving the product 
		 through this link.
		Note that when reassigning the implementer, the transport controllers 
		 usually modify the link's properties immediately in event handlers.

properties.name: SupportedGroup
properties.desc:
Only product types belonging to this flow group can travel 
		 through this link.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc:
Gets the properties that have vcProperty 
		 implementation.

methods.name: createTransportTarget
methods.desc:
Creates a new transport target object for this node and 
		 assigns it for the given product 
		 instance.
		The target is created with the default values of this transport 
		 node.
		Replaces any existing transport target assigned to the given 
		 product in this node.
		Note that the node automatically deletes any transport targets 
		 when they are no longer needed.

methods.name: getTransportTarget
methods.desc:
Gets transport target in this node assigned 
		 for a given product instance.
		Returns None if a target is not defined.
		Note that the node automatically deletes 
		 any transport targets when they are no longer needed.

methods.name: deleteTransportTarget
methods.desc:
Deletes a transport target assigned for a given product 
		 instance.
		Note that the default transport target is used if a product 
		 instance doesn't have a specific target defined.

methods.name: beginTransportOut
methods.desc:
Begin the process of transporting the given product 
		 through its transport solution.
		Note that transport is asynchronous i.e. the product 
		 won't leave immediately.

properties.name: TransportSystem
properties.desc: The associated transport system.

properties.name: TransportLinks
properties.desc: The transportLinks coming into, and going out from, this node.

properties.name: ProcessExecutor
properties.desc:
The associated process executor.
		This property is read only; it's value can be changed by setting 
		 the TransportNode property on a ProcessExecutor.
		(Deprecated) Should 
		 not assume 1 to 1 mapping between process executors and transport 
		 nodes and thus this property may get removed.

properties.name: ComponentContainer
properties.desc:
The component container this node monitors for arriving 
		 products.
		Using other than vcComponentContainer 
		 may cause issues.

properties.name: VisualPositionFrame
properties.desc:
Defines visualization position of the node. The frame feature 
		 must be in the same component as this transport node behavior.

properties.name: VisualPosition
properties.desc: Visualization position of this node in world coordinates.

properties.name: DefaultProductPositionFrame
properties.desc: The default position for products.

properties.name: DefaultResourcePositionFrame
properties.desc: The default position for resources.

properties.name: Frame
properties.desc:
Only used when connected to a path as sensor.
		Defines the Frame feature referenced as the sensor's physical 
		 location.

properties.name: ResetAt
properties.desc:
Only used when connected to a path as sensor.
		Defines the mode for resetting the sensor. 
		See Path Constants for more information.

properties.name: TriggerAt
properties.desc:
Only used when connected to a path as sensor.
		Defines the mode for triggering the sensor. 
		See Path Constants for more information.

methods.name: getNextLink
methods.desc:
Returns the transport link (there can be only one) that 
		 has the given transport node as its Source.
		Returns None if such link doesn't exist in the solution i.e. 
		 the route doesn't start from or pass through that transport node.

methods.name: replaceLinks
methods.desc:
Replaces the route with given links. If the given links do 
		 not form a valid transport solution, an error is raised and the 
		 previous route is preserved.

properties.name: Source
properties.desc:
The transport node this route starts from. 
		Returns None if the solution is empty.

properties.name: Destination
properties.desc:
The transport node this route ends to. 
		Returns None if the solution is empty.

properties.name: Links
properties.desc:
The list of transport links that need to be travelled to get 
		 from the Source node to the Destination node, starting from Source.

methods.name: createTransportLink
methods.desc:
Creates a new transport link from source 
		 to destination node and 
		 registers it to the system. Source 
		 and destination have 
		 to be in this transport system and cannot be the same.

methods.name: deleteTransportLink
methods.desc:
Removes the given link 
		 from this system and deletes it.

methods.name: createTransportSolution
methods.desc: Creates an empty transport solution.

methods.name: findSolution
methods.desc:
Tries to find a valid route from source 
		 to destination, only 
		 considers links that support the given flow group. The route isn't 
		 optimized.
		Returns None if a valid route doesn't exist.

methods.name: findAllLinksBetweenNodeSets
methods.desc:
Finds a set containing all links that are part of any valid 
		 path from any node in sourceNodes 
		 set to any node in the destinationNodes 
		 set. This can be used to e.g. check navigability between all implementations 
		 of two processes.
		The source and destination node sets can overlap.
		Only considers transport links that support the given flow group.

properties.name: ProcessController
properties.desc: Parent controller that owns this system.

properties.name: Nodes
properties.desc: Gets all transport nodes associated with this system.

properties.name: Links
properties.desc:
Gets all transport links owned 
		 by this system.

properties.name: Controllers
properties.desc:
Gets all available transport controllers. Includes both 
		 system and user-implemented controllers.

properties.name: ProductPosition
properties.desc:
Target position where a product should be placed. This matrix 
		 is expressed in world coordinates and denotes the target position 
		 and orientation of the product. Note that this is not the same 
		 as the position and orientation of the product: the difference 
		 is the offset defined in the corresponding vcProductType.

properties.name: ResourcePosition
properties.desc:
Hint for the desired location of a resource while it is 
		 placing a product instance to the ProductPosition. Expressed in 
		 world coordinates.

properties.name: ProductPositionNode
properties.desc:
By default, the node that contains 
		 ResourcePositionFrame, which is set in the transporting statement 
		 (TransportIn, 
		 TransportOut, 
		 or TransportPatternIn). 
		 If frames have not been selected, the statements use the transport 
		 node. In TransportOut, 
		 ProductPositionNode is set no None. 
		
		Reference node to ProductPositionInNode. 
		  
		Note 
		 that a reference to the vcProduct 
		 itself can be used to get the current position of the product 
		 instance at any time.

properties.name: ResourcePositionNode
properties.desc:
By default, the node that contains 
		 ResourcePositionFrame, which is set in the transporting statement 
		 (TransportIn 
		 and TransportPatternIn). 
		 If frames have not been set, the statements use the transport 
		 node. 
		  
		Reference node to ResourcePositionInNode.

properties.name: ProductPositionInNode
properties.desc:
Position in relation to ProductPositionNode, 
		 if the value of ProductPositionNode is not None. 
		  
		The property can be used to transport the product 
		 from or into moving processes or nodes.

properties.name: ResourcePositionInNode
properties.desc:
Position in relation to ResourcePositionNode, 
		 if the value of ResourcePositionNode is not None. 
		  
		The property can be used to transport the product 
		 from or into moving processes or nodes.

methods.name: addPoint
methods.desc: Adds a point to set, and then returns index of point in set.

methods.name: addTriangle
methods.desc:
Adds a triangle to set, and then returns new triangle count 
		 of set. 
		See Example. 
		 Create sphere with triangle sets for more information.

methods.name: collapsePoint
methods.desc:
Collapses a point at a given index into another point at a 
		 given index in set, thereby updating triangles referencing first 
		 point to now reference second point. 
		Generally, this is used to clean up redundant 
		 vertices, reduce data count or simplify geometry.

methods.name: convexHull
methods.desc:
Creates a convex hull from geometry of set. 
		If value is 
		 True, returns a new triangle set containing the resultant geometry.
		If value is 
		 False, modifies the current geometry of set and returns the same 
		 set.

methods.name: decimate
methods.desc:
Simplifies triangles of set by merging points within a given 
		 maxError tolerance until a given quality level is achieved or tolerance is 
		 exceeded.

methods.name: decompose
methods.desc:
Regroups triangles in set into different sets based on the 
		 connection of each triangle to one another.

methods.name: deleteTriangle
methods.desc:
Deletes a triangle at a given index 
		 in set. 
		You should call the update() method after 
		 deleting one or more triangles from set.

methods.name: getClosestPointAndNormal
methods.desc:
Returns the closest point 
		 to a given referencePoint in 
		 the set. The object coordinate system of the set is used to find 
		 the point, which is returned along with its surface normal.

methods.name: getTexCoord1
methods.desc: Returns the texture coordinates of a point at a given index in set.

methods.name: getTextureCoordinates
methods.desc:
Returns a list containing 
		 an ordered pair of UV coordinates for points at given indices 
		 in set.

methods.name: getPoint
methods.desc:
Returns the position vector of point at a given index 
		 in set.

methods.name: getPointIndexesWithin
methods.desc:
Returns a list of indices 
		 for points in set within an area defined by a given position 
		 and side_length. 
		A normal argument 
		 can be given to filter points with the same surface normal.
		See 
		 Example. 
		 Get position of points for more information.

methods.name: getPointNormals
methods.desc:
Returns a list of surface 
		 normal vectors for points at a given list of indices 
		 in set. 
		A convert argument 
		 can be used to transform each vector by a given matrix.

methods.name: getPointPositions
methods.desc:
Returns a list of position 
		 vectors for points at a given list of indices 
		 in set. 
		A convert argument 
		 can be used to transform each vector by a given matrix.

methods.name: getTriangle
methods.desc: Returns the indices of vertices for a triangle at a given index in set.

methods.name: getTriangleEdgeNeighbor
methods.desc:
Returns the index of a triangle neighboring another triangle 
		 at a given index and vertex 
		 in set. 
		The vertex argument 
		 should be either 0, 1 or 2.
		The returned value is an ordered pair identifying 
		 neighboring triangle and shared vertex in set.

methods.name: getTriangleEdgeType
methods.desc:
Returns the type of edge for a triangle at a given index 
		 and vertex in set. 
		The vertex argument 
		 should be either 0, 1 or 2.
		The returned type is one of seven possibilities:
		0 = UNKOWN
		Type is unknown.
		1 = LINE
		No triangle attached to edge.
		2 = CO_PLANAR
		Two triangles attached to edge and their surface normals are parallel.
		3 = SOFT
		Two triangles attached to edge and angle between surface normals 
		 is within angle tolerance of set, that is smooth surface.
		4 = HARD
		Two triangles attached to edge and angle between surface normals 
		 is outside angle tolerance of set, that is coarse surface.
		5 = BOUNDARY
		One triangle attached to edge.
		6 = NON_MANIFOLD
		More than two triangles attached to edge.

methods.name: getTriangleNormal
methods.desc:
Returns the surface normal of a triangle at a given index 
		 in set.

methods.name: mergePoints
methods.desc:
Merges points of triangles within a given tolerance 
		 that are not connected to one another by adding lines. 
		A onlyBoundaryPoints 
		 argument can be used to only merge points that border one another 
		 and that are within the given tolerance.

methods.name: setPoint
methods.desc:
Sets the position vector of a point at a given index 
		 in set.

methods.name: setTexCoord1
methods.desc: Sets the texture coordinates of a point at a given index in set.

methods.name: setTextureCoordinates
methods.desc:
Sets the texture coordinates 
		 of points at a given list of indices 
		 in set.

methods.name: setTriangle
methods.desc:
Sets the vertex indices of a triangle at a given index 
		 in set.

methods.name: subdivide
methods.desc:
Modifies triangles in set into smaller triangles with edge 
		 lengths smaller or equal to a given max_edge_length. 
		 
		A max_triangles 
		 argument can be given to stop subdivision when triangle count 
		 reaches a maximum limit.

methods.name: update
methods.desc: Updates the set and its bound box.

properties.name: CreaseAngle
properties.desc:
Defines angle tolerance for triangle edge shading in which 
		 edge angles less than tolerance are rendered as smooth surfaces 
		 during light calculations.

properties.name: DynamicTextureCoordinates1
properties.desc:
Defines if texture coordinates of set can be updated during 
		 simulation.

properties.name: DynamicUpdate
properties.desc: Defines if geometry of set can be updated during simulation.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc: Defines the name of set.

properties.name: PointCount
properties.desc: Gets the total number of points in set.

properties.name: PolygonCount
properties.desc: Gets the total number of triangles in set.

properties.name: PolygonTable
properties.desc:
Defines a polygon table in the form of an ordered list used 
		 for generating triangles of set. 
		In order to generate triangles, the vertex 
		 count of polygon is given first followed by the index for each 
		 vertex and so on for each subsequent polygon. For example, [3,0,1,2,3,0,2,3] 
		 would define two polygons with each having three vertices in which 
		 two are shared. Any polygon with four or more vertices will be 
		 tessellated.
		The actual positions of vertices are defined 
		 in PositionTable.
		See Example. 
		 Use polygon table to generate triangles for more information.

properties.name: PositionTable
properties.desc:
Defines a position table in the form of an ordered list used 
		 for generating triangles of set. 
		In order to generate triangles, position 
		 values should have a known index and be in XYZ order. For example, 
		 [123.0,45.0,4.5,15.0,45.0,90.0] would define the position of two 
		 points which are aligned on Y-axis.
		If the number of entries is not enough for 
		 all points in set, those points will be deleted from set as a 
		 clean up operation.
		If number is more than is needed for points, 
		 additional points are created in set.

properties.name: TextureCoordinateTable
properties.desc:
Gets/Sets texture coordinates for points in set. 
		f the number of entries is not enough for 
		 all points in set, those points will be deleted from set as a 
		 clean up operation.
		If number is more than is needed for points, 
		 additional points are created in set.

properties.name: Topology
properties.desc: Gets the container of topology data for points in set.

properties.name: TriangleCount
properties.desc: Gets the total number of triangles in set.

properties.name: TriangleTable
properties.desc:
Gets/Sets the triangle table of set, which is an ordered list 
		 of vertex indices for each triangle.

properties.name: UseTextureCoordinates1
properties.desc: Turns on/off the use of texture coordinates in set.

methods.name: convertFromCanonical
methods.desc:
Converts a given canonical value to a unit value, and then 
		 returns the unit value.

methods.name: convertToCanonical
methods.desc:
Converts a given unit value to a canonical value, and then 
		 returns the canonical value.

methods.name: getConstantExpression
methods.desc:
Converts a given canonical value to a unit value, and then 
		 returns an expression of unit value with an appended unit specification.

methods.name: getRelativeMagnitude
methods.desc:
Returns the size of unit in relation to a given magnitude using 
		 a logarithm of unit factor and a given magnitude 
		 which must be greater than zero.

properties.name: Factor
properties.desc:
If unit is built-in, gets conversion factor; otherwise defines 
		 conversion factor. That is, the size of unit in canonical units 
		 which must be larger than zero.

properties.name: Group
properties.desc:
Gets the unit group of unit, which is defined at the time of 
		 unit creation.

properties.name: IsBuiltIn
properties.desc: Indicates if unit is built-in.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc:
If unit is built-in, gets the unit's name; otherwise defines 
		 the name of unit.

properties.name: Offset
properties.desc:
If unit is built-in, gets zero-point offset; otherwise defines 
		 the canonical value at which the unit value is zero.

properties.name: Suffix
properties.desc:
If built-in, gets unit's suffix; otherwise defines the suffix 
		 of unit , which is displayed in GUI with property values.

methods.name: addGroup
methods.desc:
Adds a given unit group or one matching a given name to unit 
		 family, and then returns the index of unit group in unit family.

methods.name: containsGroup
methods.desc:
Returns True if a given unit group or one matching a given 
		 name is in the unit family; otherwise returns False.

methods.name: removeGroup
methods.desc:
Removes a given unit group or one matching a given name from 
		 unit family.
		Returns True if removal is successful; otherwise 
		 returns False if name does not match a unit group or throws an 
		 exception if unit group is built-in.

methods.name: removeGroupAt
methods.desc:
Removes a unit group at a given index from unit family.
		This method throws an exception if unit 
		 group is built-in.

properties.name: Groups
properties.desc: Gets a list of all unit groups in unit family.

properties.name: IsBuiltIn
properties.desc:
Indicates if unit family is a built-in type.
		If True, adding and removing custom unit 
		 groups from unit family is allowed but not for built-in unit groups.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc:
If unit family is built-in, gets the unit family's name; otherwise 
		 defines the name of unit family which cannot contain any dot (.) 
		 characters.

methods.name: createUnit
methods.desc:
If not a built-in unit group, adds a new unit of a given name and suffix 
		 to unit group, and then returns the index of new unit in unit 
		 group.
		If built-in unit group, throws an exception.

methods.name: deleteUnitAt
methods.desc:
If not a built-in unit group, removes a unit at a given index in unit group.
		If built-in unit group, throws an exception.

methods.name: getUnitWithMagnitude
methods.desc: Returns a unit in unit group that best matches a given magnitude.

properties.name: IsBuiltIn
properties.desc: Indicates if unit group is a built-in group.

properties.name: Name
properties.desc:
If unit group is built-in, gets the unit group's name; otherwise 
		 defines the name of unit group which cannot contain any dot (.) 
		 characters.

properties.name: Quantity
properties.desc: Gets the quantity referencing unit group.

properties.name: Units
properties.desc: Gets a list of all units in unit group.

methods.name: W
methods.desc: Defines w-component (fourth element) of vector.

methods.name: X
methods.desc: Defines x-component (first element) of vector.

methods.name: Y
methods.desc: Defines y-component (second element) of vector.

methods.name: Z
methods.desc: Defines z-component (third element) of vector.

methods.name: angle
methods.desc: Returns the angle (in radians) between vector and a given vector.

methods.name: getQuaternionAngle
methods.desc: Returns the quaternion angle between vector and a given vector.

methods.name: length
methods.desc: Returns the magnitude (length) of vector.

methods.name: normalize
methods.desc: Normalizes vector.

methods.name: square
methods.desc: Returns the square of vector.

properties.name: new
properties.access:
vcVector vector 
		 
		or
		Real x, Real 
		 y, Real z
		or
		Real x, Real 
		 y, Real z, 
		 Real w
		or
		[no argument]
properties.desc:
Creates a new vcVector object. 
		One option allows you to give an existing 
		 vector, thereby creating a copy.
		A second option allows you to give three 
		 components for new vector.
		A third option allows you to give four components 
		 for new vector.
		A fourth option allows you to give no arguments, 
		 thereby creating a zero vector.

properties.name: IsAngular
properties.desc:
Defines if vector quantity is angular or Cartesian type. 
If quantity is built-in, you can only get value.

properties.name: Pair
properties.desc:
Defines a vector quantity paired with the quantity in order 
		 to be used as matrix properties. 
		If IsAngular is set to True, pair must be 
		 a Cartesian vector quantity; otherwise the pair must be an angular 
		 vector quantity.
		If quantity is built-in, you can only get 
		 value.

properties.name: VectorName
properties.desc:
Defines an alternative name for quantity instead of its inherited 
		 Name property. 
		If value is None or empty string, quantity 
		 uses its inherited Name property.

properties.name: CameraFar
properties.desc: Defines the distance of far clipping plane from camera location.

properties.name: CameraFovy
properties.desc: Defines the field of view (in degrees) for camera.

properties.name: CameraIsOrtho
properties.desc: Turns on/off orthographic mode in camera.

properties.name: CameraMatrix
properties.desc: Defines the location of camera in World coordinate system.

properties.name: CameraNear
properties.desc: Defines the distance of near clipping plane from camera location.

properties.name: Flags
properties.desc:
Defines if camera, light and shading settings are stored in view.
		0
		Include none.
		1
		Include camera.
		2
		Include lights.
		3
		Include camera and lights.
		4
		Include shading.
		5
		Include camera and shading.
		6
		Include lights and shading.
		7
Include camera, lights and shading.

properties.name: Properties
properties.desc: Gets a list of all properties for view.

properties.name: ShadingEdge
properties.desc:
Defines the shading mode of view. 
		0
		No edges.
		1
		All edges.
		2
		Hard edges.
		3
		Silhouette edges (Currently not implemented).
		4
		Edge analysis.

properties.name: ShadingRender
properties.desc:
Defines rendering mode of view. 
		0
		No rendering.
		1
		Bounding boxes.
		2
		No filling.
		3
		Background.
		4
		Constant filling (Currently not implemented).
		5
		Flat shaded.
		6
		Smooth shaded.

methods.name: getProgram
methods.desc: Returns the program of animator.

properties.name: Program
properties.desc: Gets the program of animator.

methods.name: getHitFeature
methods.desc:
Returns a feature at a given index 
		 in detected collisions list.

methods.name: getHitGeometrySet
methods.desc:
Returns a geometry set at a given index 
		 in detected collisions list.

methods.name: getHitNode
methods.desc: Returns a node at a given index in detected collisions list.

methods.name: testAllCollisions
methods.desc:
Detects all collisions of box with node list. 
		An optional tolerance 
		 argument can be given to detect collisions within a certain distance. 
		 By default, tolerance is zero.
		If a collision is detected, returns True; 
		 otherwise returns False.

methods.name: testOneCollision
methods.desc:
Detects the first collision of box with node list. 
		An optional tolerance 
		 argument can be given to detect collisions within a certain distance. 
		 By default, tolerance is zero.
		If a collision is detected, returns True; 
		 otherwise returns False.
